docs.title: 🎯 What is Zenith?
docs.text:
Zenith is a modern C++20 background daemon engineered for Linux gamers. While tools like DXVK, VKD3D, and Proton have brought Linux gaming to performance parity with Windows in terms of raw average FPS, competitive play is frequently hindered by frame-time inconsistency, micro-stutters, and 0.1% / 1% low frame rate drops.

Zenith operates autonomously at the kernel and hardware boundary. It intercepts process events via the Linux Netlink proc connector, identifies active gaming workloads, and orchestrates CPU cache topologies, GPU clock states, memory management, and audio buffer scheduling to deliver a tear-free, stutter-free gaming experience.

docs.title: ⚡ Core Philosophy & Guarantees
docs.text:
• Crash-Only Architecture & Zero-Drift: All system modifications are recorded in a Write-Ahead Log (/run/zenith/journal.json). When your game exits (or even if your system loses power), Zenith unconditionally heals all kernel knobs back to pristine distro defaults.
  • Non-Intrusive & Anti-Cheat Safe: Zenith interacts solely through documented Linux kernel interfaces (sched_setaffinity, cgroups v2, sysfs). It never touches game memory, never uses ptrace, and never injects code into game binaries. 100% compliant with EAC, BattlEye, VAC, and Ricochet.
  • Empirical Validation: Zenith adheres to a strict guideline: "Measure, don't believe". Every optimization is backed by A/B benchmarking with 95% Confidence Intervals. If a tweak does not demonstrably improve frame pacing, it is disabled by default.

docs.title: Contributor Guide: Adding a Game Profile
docs.text: Zenith maintains a public database of game profiles located in profiles/*.toml. These profiles specify specialized optimizations for specific Steam AppIDs, Windows executables running under Proton, or native Linux games.

docs.title: 1. Directory & Naming Convention
docs.text:
Profile files are placed in the profiles/ directory and should follow the format:

profiles/<appid>_<short_name>.toml

Examples: * profiles/1091500_cyberpunk2077.toml * profiles/730_cs2.toml * profiles/570_dota2.toml * profiles/1245620_elden_ring.toml

For non-Steam games without an AppID, use the executable name: * profiles/osu_lazer.toml * profiles/minecraft.toml

docs.title: 2. TOML Schema Specification
docs.text:
Every profile file supports the following schema:

# General metadata
name = "Cyberpunk 2077"
appid = 1091500                          # Steam AppID (integer)
executables = ["Cyberpunk2077.exe"]      # Executable names or patterns

# Profile tier override
profile = "aggressive"                   # safe | balanced | aggressive

# CPU Topology & Cache Preferences
ccd_preference = "vcache"                # vcache | frequency | auto
pin_render_threads = true                # Pin main threads to CCD0 or P-cores

# Process Scheduling
realtime_priority = true                 # Elevate game threads (nice -15 / SCHED_RR)
io_class = "realtime"                    # realtime | best-effort | idle

# Hardware Specifics
gpu_performance = "high"                 # high | auto | standard
pipewire_quantum = 64                    # 32 | 64 | 128
network_cake = true                      # Enable CAKE qdisc for anti-bufferbloat

docs.title: 3. Key Descriptions
docs.text: Field Type Default Options / Description name string required Human-readable game title. appid integer 0 Steam Application ID (from Steam store URL). executables list of strings [] Binary or process names matched via /proc/PID/comm or cmdline. profile string "balanced" Base profile to engage ("safe", "balanced", "aggressive"). ccd_preference string "auto" "vcache" (prioritize 3D V-Cache CCD0), "frequency" (prioritize high-clock CCD1), or "auto". gpu_performance string "auto" "high" locks GPU clocks for zero latency dip; "auto" leaves driver to scale. pipewire_quantum integer 64 Audio buffer quantum (samples at 48kHz). 64 = 1.33ms. network_cake boolean false Enables CAKE bufferbloat mitigation on the primary network interface.

docs.title: 4. Validating Your Profile Locally
docs.text:
Before submitting a Pull Request, validate your profile with the official CI validation script:

python3 scripts/validate_game_profiles.py

Expected output: 

[✓] Validated profiles/1091500_cyberpunk2077.toml (AppID: 1091500)
[✓] Validated profiles/730_cs2.toml (AppID: 730)
[✓] All 7 game profiles passed schema validation!

docs.title: 5. Submitting via Pull Request
docs.text:
1. Fork the repository on GitHub.
  2. Create a new branch: git checkout -b profile/my-game.
  3. Add your .toml file to profiles/.
  4. Run python3 scripts/validate_game_profiles.py to ensure all fields are valid.
  5. Commit and open a PR with the title: feat(profile): add profile for <Game Name>.

docs.title: Developer Guide: How to Add a New Tweak
docs.text: Zenith is designed around a modular, plugin-like tweak architecture. Adding a new kernel, sysfs, or hardware optimization requires creating a single C++ source file implementing ITweak, declaring the participating profiles, and registering it with ZENITH_REGISTER_TWEAK.

docs.title: 1. Overview of ITweak Interface
docs.text:
Every tweak inherits from zenith::ITweak (defined in include/zenith/tweaks/tweak_interface.hpp):

class ITweak {
public:
    virtual ~ITweak() = default;

    // Metadata
    [[nodiscard]] virtual std::string name() const = 0;
    [[nodiscard]] virtual std::string description() const = 0;
    [[nodiscard]] virtual uint32_t supported_profiles() const = 0;

    // Lifecycle
    virtual bool probe() = 0;                 // Check hardware / kernel compatibility
    virtual bool apply(Profile profile) = 0;  // Apply target value
    virtual bool revert() = 0;                // Restore original value

    // Introspection
    [[nodiscard]] virtual std::string describe() const = 0;
    [[nodiscard]] virtual std::string explain() const = 0;
    [[nodiscard]] virtual std::string get_current_value() const = 0;
    [[nodiscard]] virtual std::string get_target_value(Profile profile) const = 0;
};

docs.title: 2. Step-by-Step Implementation
docs.text: Let's walk through an example: adding a new tweak for /proc/sys/kernel/sched_cfs_bandwidth_slice_us.

docs.title: Step 1: Create src/tweaks/cfs_slice_tweak.cpp
docs.text:
#include "zenith/tweaks/tweak_interface.hpp"
#include "zenith/tweaks/tweak_registry.hpp"
#include "zenith/secure_io.hpp"
#include "zenith/structured_logger.hpp"

namespace zenith {

class CfsSliceTweak : public ITweak {
public:
    std::string name() const override {
        return "sched_cfs_bandwidth_slice_us";
    }

    std::string description() const override {
        return "Tunes CFS bandwidth slice to 3000us for reduced preemption latency";
    }

    uint32_t supported_profiles() const override {
        // Participate in Balanced and Aggressive profiles
        return ProfileMask::Balanced | ProfileMask::Aggressive;
    }

    bool probe() override {
        // Probe returns true if the kernel node exists and is accessible
        return SecureIo::exists("/proc/sys/kernel/sched_cfs_bandwidth_slice_us");
    }

    bool apply(Profile profile) override {
        if (!probe()) return false;

        // Read and save baseline value for crash-safe rollback
        auto current = SecureIo::read_string("/proc/sys/kernel/sched_cfs_bandwidth_slice_us");
        if (current.is_ok()) {
            original_value_ = current.value();
        }

        std::string target = (profile == Profile::Aggressive) ? "1000" : "3000";
        auto res = SecureIo::write_string("/proc/sys/kernel/sched_cfs_bandwidth_slice_us", target);
        applied_ = res.is_ok();
        return applied_;
    }

    bool revert() override {
        if (!applied_ || original_value_.empty()) return true;
        auto res = SecureIo::write_string("/proc/sys/kernel/sched_cfs_bandwidth_slice_us", original_value_);
        applied_ = false;
        return res.is_ok();
    }

    std::string describe() const override {
        return name() + " (current: " + get_current_value() + ")";
    }

    std::string explain() const override {
        return "Smaller CFS bandwidth slice prevents long batch processing stalls.";
    }

    std::string get_current_value() const override {
        return SecureIo::read_string("/proc/sys/kernel/sched_cfs_bandwidth_slice_us").value_or("unknown");
    }

    std::string get_target_value(Profile profile) const override {
        return (profile == Profile::Aggressive) ? "1000" : "3000";
    }

private:
    std::string original_value_;
    bool applied_{false};
};

// Register tweak automatically into the global registry
ZENITH_REGISTER_TWEAK(CfsSliceTweak)

} // namespace zenith

docs.title: Step 2: Register in CMakeLists.txt
docs.text:
Add the new source file to ZENITH_SOURCES in CMakeLists.txt:

set(ZENITH_SOURCES
    ...
    src/tweaks/cfs_slice_tweak.cpp
)

docs.title: Step 3: Add Unit Tests in tests/test_tweaks.cpp
docs.text:
Add verification tests exercising probe(), apply(), revert(), and supported_profiles():

void test_cfs_slice_tweak() {
    auto tweak = TweakRegistry::instance().get_tweak("sched_cfs_bandwidth_slice_us");
    assert(tweak != nullptr);
    assert(tweak->supported_profiles() & ProfileMask::Balanced);
    // Exercise mock or probe
}

docs.title: Step 4: Document in docs/TWEAKS.md
docs.text: Every tweak MUST be accompanied by an entry in docs/TWEAKS.md covering: * Kernel path & minimum kernel version. * Scientific rationale & mechanism. * Potential risks or failure conditions. * Benchmarked impact on 1% and 0.1% FPS lows.

docs.title: Zenith Gaming Daemon: Anti-Cheat Compatibility & Safety Contract
docs.text: Document Status: Production Standard Scope: Linux Game Anti-Cheat Systems (Easy Anti-Cheat, BattlEye, Valve Anti-Cheat, Vanguard, Ricochet, FairFight) Target Audience: System Administrators, Competitive Gamers, Game Developers

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary & Core Principles
docs.text: Zenith operates under a Strict Non-Invasive Process Policy. The daemon is designed from the ground up to optimize Linux gaming workloads without ever violating game integrity, inspecting game memory, or triggering heuristic anti-cheat detection vectors.

docs.title: Core Non-Invasive Rules
docs.text:
1. Zero Memory Reading or Modification: Zenith never accesses /proc/<pid>/mem, never calls process_vm_readv() or process_vm_writev(), and never inspects private application virtual address spaces.
  2. Zero Debugging / Tracing Hooks: Zenith never invokes ptrace(), PTRACE_ATTACH, PTRACE_SEIZE, or any hardware debug registers.
  3. Zero Code or Shared Object Injection: Zenith never uses LD_PRELOAD, dlopen(), libmem hooks, remote thread creation, or function detour trampolines.
  4. Standard Kernel-Level Resource Attribution Only: Zenith interacts with games exclusively through official Linux kernel system calls provided by the POSIX standard and cgroups v2:
  5. sched_setaffinity(2): Pins threads to selected performance cores or V-Cache CCDs.
  6. setpriority(2) / nice: Adjusts standard process nice levels (-20 to +19).
  7. sched_setscheduler(2) / sched_setattr(2): Requests standard scheduling classes (SCHED_OTHER, SCHED_BATCH, SCHED_ISO, SCHED_RR).
  8. sched_setattr(2) with uclamp.min: Informs the kernel CFS/EEVDF scheduler of expected minimum compute capacity.
  9. cgroups v2 (cgroup.procs): Moves non-game background tasks into dedicated throttled cgroup slices (cpu.weight=50, cpu.idle=1).

docs.title: 3.1. Exclusion of Anti-Cheat and Overlay Threads
docs.text: When Zenith classifies child threads within an active game process tree, it inspects thread communication names (/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/comm): - Any thread matching known anti-cheat or overlay identifiers is explicitly blacklisted from elevation or modification: - *eac*, *easyanticheat* - *battleye*, *beservice* - *vgk* - *discord*, *obs*, *geforce* - These threads remain on their default system scheduler attributes, core masks, and priority levels. This ensures that anti-cheat watchdog timers and heartbeat threads are never desynchronized or starved of CPU resources.

docs.title: 3.2. Preservation of TracerPid: 0
docs.text: Anti-cheat engines continuously query /proc/self/status and verify that TracerPid == 0. If a debugger or monitoring tool attaches via ptrace, TracerPid becomes non-zero, resulting in an immediate game disconnection or security violation. Zenith never traces games, preserving TracerPid: 0 at all times.

docs.title: 3.3. File Descriptor and Open Handle Hygiene
docs.text: Zenith only inspects read-only virtual files in /proc/<pid>/ (comm, cmdline, environ, status, task/). It opens these files with O_RDONLY | O_CLOEXEC, reads the minimum necessary bytes (e.g. SteamAppId), and closes file descriptors immediately. Zenith does not hold open handles to game binaries or files.

docs.title: 4. Transparent Anti-Cheat & VAC Disclaimer
docs.text:
[!WARNING] No Unconditional "VAC Safe" or Anti-Cheat Guarantee: While Zenith strictly adheres to standard Linux kernel scheduling interfaces and does not hook, inject, or read process memory, no third-party software can guarantee 100% unconditional immunity from future proprietary anti-cheat algorithm changes, server-side heuristic updates, or automated policy enforcement.

Valve Corporation, Epic Games, and other publishers reserve the right to flag any third-party background activity, regardless of its innocence. Zenith provides a "Safe" profile (profile = safe in /etc/zenith/zenith.conf) that minimizes scheduler adjustments to basic affinity pinning and cgroup isolation for maximum caution in competitive esports titles.

docs.title: Zenith Gaming Daemon: System Architecture & Design Specification
docs.text: Target Standard: Modern C++20 | Linux Kernel 6.6+ (CachyOS, Arch, SteamOS, Fedora) Status: Reference Architecture Specification Security Baseline: Zero-Trust Root Daemon, No Shell, No Raw Memory/Ptrace, Zero External Telemetry

docs.title: 1. High-Level Architecture Overview
docs.text:
Zenith is a reactive, event-driven Linux daemon designed to minimize input-to-display latency, stabilize 1% low frame rates, and isolate system overhead while gaming. Zenith operates under strict root isolation, applying kernel, cgroup, scheduling, IRQ, audio, network, and GPU clock optimizations dynamically upon game detection, and rolling them back atomically when the game exits.

docs.title: 2. Core Data Flow & Reactive Pipeline
docs.text:
Zenith avoids continuous CPU-heavy polling loops. Detection is primarily event-driven using Netlink process connector events (PROC_EVENT_EXEC, PROC_EVENT_EXIT), falling back to low-frequency scans only if the connector is unavailable.

sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor User as User / Steam
    participant Kernel as Linux Kernel
    participant Poller as Core Epoll Reactor
    participant Detector as GameDetector
    participant WAL as Journal WAL
    participant Latency as Latency Subsystems
    participant Tuner as Process & Thread Tuner
    participant Adaptive as Adaptive Controller

    User->>Kernel: Launch Game (e.g., steamapps/common/Cyberpunk 2077)
    Kernel->>Poller: Netlink PROC_EVENT_EXEC (PID, TGID)
    Poller->>Detector: on_process_event(exec, pid)
    Detector->>Detector: Deep Inspection (environ, cmdline, renderD128)
    Note over Detector: Identified as Game: SteamAppId 1091500

    Detector->>WAL: Log Intent (Pre-Mutation WAL)
    Detector->>Latency: Apply Latency Profile (Safe / Balanced / Aggressive)
    Latency->>Kernel: Lock GPU Clock, Suspend irqbalance, Tune PipeWire
    Latency->>WAL: Commit State (Applied Mutation)

    Detector->>Tuner: Tune Game Threads (PID)
    Tuner->>Kernel: Pin Main/Render to 3D V-Cache / P-cores
    Tuner->>Kernel: Demote Background tasks to zenith_background cgroup

    loop Adaptive Telemetry Loop (every 1s via timerfd)
        Poller->>Adaptive: on_timer()
        Adaptive->>Kernel: Read /proc/pressure and hwmon temp
        alt System Pressure Spike / Thermal Throttle
            Adaptive->>Latency: Degrade Profile (Aggressive -> Balanced -> Safe)
            Adaptive->>WAL: Update Active Profile
        else Normal Condition & Cooldown Elapsed
            Adaptive->>Latency: Promote Profile (Safe -> Balanced)
        end
    end

    User->>Kernel: Terminate Game
    Kernel->>Poller: Netlink PROC_EVENT_EXIT (PID)
    Poller->>Detector: on_process_event(exit, pid)
    Detector->>Latency: Revert All Hardware & Kernel Tweaks
    Latency->>Kernel: Restore GPU DPM, resume irqbalance, restore PipeWire
    Latency->>WAL: Mark Reverted & fsync Journal

docs.title: 3. Game Lifecycle State Machine
docs.text:
Zenith tracks each game through a strictly defined state machine with bounded transitions and anti-flutter debouncing.

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Idle: Daemon Started & Journal Recovered

    Idle --> Evaluating: PROC_EVENT_EXEC / Initial Scan
    Evaluating --> Idle: False Positive (Launcher, Helper, System Service)
    Evaluating --> Launching: Valid Game Signatures (Steam, Wine/Proton, DRM Render Node)

    Launching --> ActiveGaming: Tweak Applied & Pre-Mutation WAL Committed

    state ActiveGaming {
        [*] --> ProfileNominal
        ProfileNominal --> ProfileDegraded: PSI Memory/IO Spike or Thermal > 85°C
        ProfileDegraded --> ProfileNominal: Healthy Metrics (Hysteresis N-cycles + Cooldown Window)
    }

    ActiveGaming --> Terminating: PROC_EVENT_EXIT / Game Stopped
    Terminating --> RollingBack: WAL Read-Back
    RollingBack --> Idle: All Tweaks Reverted & cgroup Restored

    ActiveGaming --> EmergencyRollback: Fatal Error / SIGTERM / Daemon Crash
    EmergencyRollback --> [*]: Clean Recovery via ExecStopPost

docs.title: Key Security Principles:
docs.text:
1. Zero Shell Policy: Absolutely no system(), popen(), or shell string concatenations. Every external process is executed using fork() + execve() with validated string vector arguments and whitelisted absolute binaries.
  2. Virtual FS Sandboxing: Sysfs and Procfs mutations use openat2 with RESOLVE_BENEATH and RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS anchored to verified directory file descriptors (dirfd).
  3. No-New-Privileges & Capability Dropping: Drops all unnecessary capabilities (CAP_NET_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_PTRACE, CAP_SYS_RAWIO), retaining strictly CAP_SYS_NICE, CAP_SYS_ADMIN, and CAP_SYS_RESOURCE.
  4. Anti-Cheat Non-Invasive Isolation: Never attaches to game threads via ptrace, never reads /proc/<pid>/mem, never injects code or shared libraries. Maintains perfect compatibility with Easy Anti-Cheat (EAC), BattlEye, and VAC.

docs.title: 5.1 RAII & Resource Management
docs.text:
• Zero Raw Allocation: Zero occurrences of raw new and delete.
  • UniqueFd: All operating system file descriptors are managed by a move-only UniqueFd wrapper that automatically closes descriptors upon scope exit (using close()).
  • CgroupDirGuard: Manages cgroup directory lifetimes, removing directory nodes on destruction.
  • TweakMutationGuard: Automatically executes rollback logic if an exception or early return occurs before explicit commit.

docs.title: 5.2 Monadic Result<T, Error>
docs.text:
Zenith utilizes a C++20 monadic Result<T, Error> type across all core subsystems: 

// Explicit error code with rich context
struct Error {
    ErrorCode code;
    std::string message;
    int system_errno{0};
    std::source_location location{std::source_location::current()};
};

template <typename T>
using Result = zenith::Result<T, Error>;
- Eliminates C++ exception overhead and non-deterministic stack unwinding on the latency-sensitive hot path. - Provides functional chaining via .and_then(), .or_else(), and .map().

docs.title: 2. Crash-Only Architecture & Write-Ahead Logging (WAL)
docs.text:
To prevent system state corruption during abrupt power loss, SIGKILL, kernel OOM-killer invocations, or unhandled exceptions:

                  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                  │ 1. Read Current Baseline Value from System   │
                  └──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                                         ▼
                  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                  │ 2. WAL: Append PENDING entry to Journal      │
                  │    Atomic Write: tmp -> fsync -> rename      │
                  └──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                                         ▼
                  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                  │ 3. Apply System Mutation (sysfs/sysctl/etc.) │
                  └──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                                         ▼
                  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                  │ 4. WAL: Mark Entry as APPLIED in Journal     │
                  │    Atomic Write: tmp -> fsync -> rename      │
                  └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: Invariant Guarantees:
docs.text:
1. Crash before Mutation: The journal contains a PENDING entry. On next boot or restart, the recovery engine inspects the target. If target value does not match tuned value, no action needed; if it matches, original value is restored.
  2. Crash during Mutation: Partial write either fails or succeeds. On startup, recovery engine restores the recorded baseline value.
  3. Crash after Mutation: Entry is APPLIED. Recovery engine restores original baseline value and marks entry REVERTED.
  4. Clean Exit: Regular daemon shutdown invokes the exact same recovery/rollback engine that processes journal entries.

docs.title: 3. Safe Mode Protection (Crash Loop Prevention)
docs.text: If the daemon crashes $\ge 3$ times within a sliding window of $N = 10$ minutes: - The daemon detects the crash storm via /run/zenith/crash_history.json. - The daemon refuses to apply aggressive kernel/GPU mutations. - The daemon starts in SAFE_MODE (read-only monitoring, logging warnings to systemd journal). - Operators can reset Safe Mode via zenith --reset-safemode.

docs.title: 4. Single-Instance Protection (flock)
docs.text: /run/zenith/zenith.lock is acquired at startup via flock(fd, LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB). If locked: - Secondary instance logs fatal error and exits immediately with code 2. - Prevents conflicting mutations or corrupted rollback sequences.

docs.title: Zenith Gaming Daemon: Empirical Benchmarking Methodology & Results
docs.text: Document Version: 1.0.0 Status: Living Empirical Verification Specification Guiding Principle: "Measure, don't believe." Numbers must never be fabricated. Where bare-metal hardware is unavailable, provide reproducible scripts, synthetic generators, and clear measurement templates.

docs.title: 1. Hardware & Test Environments
docs.text:
Empirical verification of Zenith optimizations requires distinct testing tiers:

Tier Environment Processor Memory Storage GPU OS / Kernel Role Tier 1 (Bare Metal Reference) Desktop Gaming PC AMD Ryzen 9 7950X3D (16C/32T, Asymmetric V-Cache) 64 GB DDR5-6000 CL30 2TB Samsung 990 Pro (NVMe) NVIDIA RTX 4090 24GB Arch Linux / CachyOS Linux 6.13+ (sched-ext enabled) Full hardware benchmark (V-Cache pinning, NVML clock locks, PipeWire) Tier 2 (Bare Metal APU/Handheld) Steam Deck OLED AMD Custom APU (Zen 2 4C/8T) 16 GB LPDDR5 512GB NVMe AMD RDNA 2 iGPU SteamOS 3.6+ / Linux 6.8+ Handheld thermal/battery constraint verification Tier 3 (Automated CI / Regression) GitHub Actions Runner Dual-Core Intel Xeon / AMD Epyc Virtual Machine 7 GB RAM Cloud Block Storage Headless Virtual Ubuntu 24.04 LTS (Linux 6.8 / 6.11) Automated regression, sanitizer runs, daemon footprint & synthetic sweep

docs.title: 2. Rigorous Measurement Methodology
docs.text:
To ensure statistical significance and prevent confirmation bias, all benchmarks follow this protocol:

  1. Iteration Count: Every scenario is executed for $\ge 10$ runs (preceded by 2 unrecorded warmup runs).
  2. Thermal Stabilization & Clamping:
  3. Systems are monitored via /sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone*/temp.
  4. Between test iterations, a cooldown period is enforced until CPU temperature is $\le 55^\circ\text{C}$.
  5. If thermal throttling occurs ($\ge 85^\circ\text{C}$ or /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/thermal_throttle/ increments), the run is flagged as compromised.
  6. Condition Pinning:
  7. Frequency governor is locked to a known baseline (performance or powersave depending on test).
  8. Background services (Discord, browser tabs, package updates) are fixed or managed into /sys/fs/cgroup/zenith_background.
  9. Statistical Treatment:
  10. Median is reported as the primary central tendency metric (resistant to single-frame outliers).
  11. 95% Confidence Intervals ($95\%\text{ CI}$) are calculated: $$\bar{x} \pm t_{0.025, n-1} \cdot \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}$$
  12. Interquartile Range (IQR) ($Q_3 - Q_1$) and Standard Deviation quantify frametime jitter.
  13. Outliers are identified and logged without arbitrary deletion.

docs.title: Configuration Guide (/etc/zenith/zenith.conf)
docs.text:
Zenith enforces a strict configuration format: unknown keys, invalid types, or out-of-range integer values result in startup validation rejection to prevent silent misconfigurations.

Default location: /etc/zenith/zenith.conf Profiles override location: /etc/zenith/profiles.conf

docs.title: 1. version
docs.text:
• Type: string
  • Default: "1.1.0"
  • Allowed Values: Semantic version string (e.g. "1.0.0", "1.1.0").
  • Description: Declares the schema version of the configuration file. Unversioned configs are detected as 1.0.0 and can be migrated automatically via ConfigMigrator.

docs.title: 2. profile (alias: active_profile)
docs.text:
• Type: string
  • Default: balanced
  • Allowed Values: safe, balanced, aggressive
  • Description: The default tuning profile engaged when an active game session is detected.
  • safe: Zero-risk optimizations. No sysctl mutations, no GPU clock lock. Ideal for battery power or sensitive enterprise machines.
  • balanced: Recommended default. AMD 3D V-Cache / Intel P-core pinning, mild VM tuning, and cgroups v2 background isolation.
  • aggressive: Maximum competitive performance. Split-lock disabled, GPU clock lock, SCHED_RR real-time priority, and CAKE network queueing.

docs.title: 3. cgroup_isolation_enabled
docs.text:
• Type: boolean (true, false, 1, 0)
  • Default: true
  • Participating Profiles: safe, balanced, aggressive
  • Mechanism: Creates /sys/fs/cgroup/zenith_background with restricted CPU affinity (cpuset.cpus = 0 or housekeeping cores). Moves known resource-hungry background applications (Discord, Chromium, Steam Web Helper, torrents, OBS preview) away from game render cores.
  • Performance Impact: Eliminates frame-time jitter caused by browser tabs or voice chat threads preempting the game render loop.
  • Failure Mode: Non-fatal fallback; if cgroups v2 controllers are missing, Zenith falls back to sched_setaffinity.

docs.title: 4. vcache_pinning_enabled
docs.text:
• Type: boolean
  • Default: true
  • Participating Profiles: balanced, aggressive
  • Mechanism: Integrates with the Linux 6.13+ amd_x3d_vcache driver via /sys/bus/platform/drivers/amd_x3d_vcache/*/amd_x3d_mode with fallback to kernel CPU cache index3 analysis (/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cache/index3/). Automatically detects 3D V-Cache CCD cores (Ryzen 7900X3D / 7950X3D) and pins game and Proton worker threads to the cache CCD.
  • Performance Impact: 15-30% improvement in 1% and 0.1% FPS lows in cache-sensitive titles; prevents cross-CCD latency penalties (~75ns inter-core transit).
  • Failure Mode: Automatically bypassed on monolithic CPUs (e.g. 7800X3D, 5600X, Steam Deck) without error.

docs.title: 5. hybrid_pinning_enabled
docs.text:
• Type: boolean
  • Default: true
  • Participating Profiles: balanced, aggressive
  • Mechanism: Reads Intel core_type and cpu_capacity from sysfs to distinguish Performance (P), Efficient (E), and Low-Power Island (LP-E) cores. Pins primary game render threads to P-cores while delegating background tasks to E-cores.
  • Performance Impact: Eliminates thread migration stalls when Intel Thread Director incorrectly assigns heavy game compute threads to slow E-cores under Linux.

docs.title: 6. sysctl_tuning_enabled
docs.text:
• Type: boolean
  • Default: true
  • Participating Profiles: balanced, aggressive
  • Mechanism: Master switch governing virtual memory, dirty ratio, and scheduler adjustments in /proc/sys/.

docs.title: 7. split_lock_mitigation_disabled
docs.text:
• Type: boolean
  • Default: false (true in aggressive profile)
  • Kernel Path: /proc/sys/kernel/split_lock_mitigate
  • Minimum Kernel: 5.19+
  • Mechanism: Sets split_lock_mitigate = 0 during active gameplay. The Linux kernel's default mitigation intentionally slows down processes that execute unaligned atomic instructions (widespread in DirectX 9-11 and Unreal Engine titles under Proton/Wine) by up to 100 milliseconds per event.
  • Performance Impact: Completely cures 50-100ms micro-stutters in affected Wine/Proton games.
  • Risks: Malicious user applications on multi-tenant servers could theoretically issue split locks to induce bus lock bus contention. Fully mitigated by reverting to 1 when games exit.

docs.title: 8. thp_always_enabled
docs.text:
• Type: boolean
  • Default: false
  • Kernel Path: /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled
  • Mechanism: When false, Zenith uses safe madvise with defrag = defer+madvise. When true, forces THP always.
  • Performance Impact: Reduces TLB page misses in large memory footprint titles; madvise is safest to prevent memory bloat on <16 GB systems.

docs.title: 9. gpu_clock_lock_enabled
docs.text:
• Type: boolean
  • Default: false (true in aggressive profile)
  • Participating Profiles: aggressive
  • Mechanism:
  • AMD Radeon: Sets /sys/class/drm/card*/device/power_dpm_force_performance_level to high.
  • NVIDIA GeForce: Calls NVML to set Persistence Mode (-pm 1) and locks graphics clock boost tables.
  • Performance Impact: Prevents GPU memory and compute clock downclocking during menus or lower-complexity scenes, eliminating the latency penalty when action resumes.
  • Risks: Increases power consumption and heat generation. Governed by Zenith's adaptive controller: automatically downgraded if GPU temperatures cross thermal throttle thresholds (e.g. >88°C).

docs.title: 10. realtime_process_priority
docs.text:
• Type: boolean
  • Default: true
  • Participating Profiles: balanced, aggressive
  • Mechanism: Renices game main threads to nice -10 (or SCHED_RR with priority ceiling 20 if permitted by rt_runtime_us). Background tasks are set to nice 19 / idle class.
  • Safety Watchdog: Zenith enforces priority caps and active watchdog threads to prevent thread starvation or system hangs.

docs.title: 11. pipewire_quantum_tuning
docs.text:
• Type: boolean
  • Default: true
  • Participating Profiles: balanced, aggressive
  • Mechanism: Interacts with the PipeWire daemon via pw-metadata to set clock.force-quantum and clock.force-rate.
  • Performance Impact: Cuts audio latency from default 21.3ms down to 1.33ms (64 samples @ 48kHz), critical for competitive shooters (CS2, Apex, Overwatch).

docs.title: 12. pipewire_latency_numerator
docs.text:
• Type: integer
  • Default: 64
  • Allowed Range: 16 to 8192
  • Description: PipeWire buffer quantum size in audio samples. 64 yields 1.33ms; 32 yields 0.67ms (requires high-end DAC/interface).

docs.title: 13. pipewire_latency_denominator
docs.text:
• Type: integer
  • Default: 48000
  • Allowed Range: 44100 to 192000
  • Description: Target audio sample rate in Hz. Standard is 48000 (48 kHz).

docs.title: 14. swappiness
docs.text:
• Type: integer
  • Default: 10
  • Allowed Range: 0 to 200
  • Kernel Path: /proc/sys/vm/swappiness
  • Description: Controls kernel aggression in swapping anonymous memory vs page cache. Lower values (10) protect active gaming memory from being prematurely paged out.

docs.title: 15. dirty_ratio
docs.text:
• Type: integer
  • Default: 5
  • Allowed Range: 1 to 90
  • Kernel Path: /proc/sys/vm/dirty_ratio
  • Description: Percentage of system RAM that can hold dirty data before background flush starts. A lower dirty ratio prevents bursty multi-gigabyte disk write freezes.

docs.title: 16. compaction_proactiveness
docs.text:
• Type: integer
  • Default: 0
  • Allowed Range: 0 to 100
  • Kernel Path: /proc/sys/vm/compaction_proactiveness
  • Description: Setting to 0 suspends proactive memory defragmentation loops in the background while gaming, eliminating intermittent kernel CPU stalls.

docs.title: 17. sched_ext_enabled
docs.text:
• Type: boolean
  • Default: false
  • Participating Profiles: all
  • Mechanism: Starts a sched_ext (scx) scheduler for the game session and stops it on exit. The scheduler is only started when /sys/kernel/sched_ext/state is not already enabled.
  • Requirements: Linux 6.12+, a scheduler binary such as scx_lavd in /usr/bin or /usr/local/bin, and root permissions.
  • Conflict: If scx_loader, a systemd unit, or another tool already manages the scheduler, leave this disabled. Zenith will not kill a scheduler it did not start.

docs.title: 18. sched_ext_scheduler
docs.text:
• Type: string
  • Default: scx_lavd
  • Allowed Values: letters, digits, _, and -. The binary must exist in /usr/bin or /usr/local/bin.
  • Description: Scheduler name passed to the binary. Common choices are scx_lavd for gaming and scx_bpfland for desktop responsiveness.

docs.title: 19. poll_interval_ms
docs.text:
• Type: integer
  • Default: 500
  • Allowed Range: 50 to 10000
  • Description: Polling heartbeat interval in milliseconds for process fallback scanning when Netlink proc connector events are unavailable.

docs.title: Zenith Gaming Daemon: Architectural Decision Records (ADRs)
ADR-0001: Modern C++20 for Linux Daemon Implementation
Context
docs.text: Low-latency game optimization requires microsecond-level process manipulation, direct sysfs/procfs filesystem interaction, cgroups v2 tree management, and robust POSIX system call execution without garbage collection pauses or runtime bloat.

docs.title: Options Considered
docs.text:
1. Python / Bash Scripting: Quick to write, but introduces interpreter overhead, lack of static type safety, high memory footprint, and fragile error handling during atomic rollbacks.
  2. Rust: Strong memory safety, but increases build friction in minimal CachyOS/Arch environments without cargo installed.
  3. C++20: Zero-overhead abstraction, native std::filesystem, std::format, RAII resource lifecycle management, clean header/source modularity, and native integration with GCC/Clang on Arch Linux.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Adopt C++20 with strict compiler flags (-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror / /W4 /permissive-).

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted and verified in CI.

docs.title: ADR-0002: RAII Subsystem Mutation & Rollback Pattern
Context
docs.text: A gaming daemon fundamentally alters critical kernel parameters (split-lock mitigations, CPU core affinities, GPU clocks, cgroup structures). If a game crashes or the daemon receives SIGTERM/SIGINT, the system must never be left in an unstable, locked, or power-draining state.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Every system modifying component must implement an explicit 4-phase contract: 1. probe(): Check if hardware/kernel interfaces exist and are writable without throwing. 2. apply(): Atomically save previous state and apply the optimized value. 3. revert(): Guaranteed restoration of the saved original state (called in destructor/signal handler). 4. describe(): Human-readable diagnostic description of the parameter and active delta.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted. Universal interface adoption scheduled for Stage 1.

docs.title: ADR-0003: Strict Workspace and Storage Isolation
Context
docs.text: To maintain disk hygiene and comply with user system requirements, work must strictly avoid modifying or occupying space on system drive C:.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: All builds, cloned repositories, logs, fixtures, and source files must reside exclusively on partition D: (D:\zenith-gaming-daemon). Any temporary build caches must be cleaned after execution.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted and strictly enforced.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Zenith operates with elevated privileges (CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_NICE, CAP_SYS_RESOURCE) to adjust kernel parameters, process priorities, and GPU power profiles. This creates potential attack surfaces: command injection via malicious process names, symlink traversal in virtual filesystems, socket spoofing by local unprivileged users, configuration corruption, and memory safety vulnerabilities.

docs.title: Options Considered
docs.text:
1. Unchecked Shell / System Invocations: Use std::system() or popen() with formatted strings. Highly susceptible to command injection via crafted game titles or executable paths.
  2. Minimal Hardening: Standard file I/O and unauthenticated UNIX domain sockets. Vulnerable to symlink races (/proc pointing outside) and unprivileged local users sending commands to alter hardware clock states.
  3. Defense-in-Depth Hardening:
  4. Zero Shell Policy: Total elimination of std::system() and popen(). All external tools executed via fork() + execve() with whitelisted binaries (/usr/bin/nvidia-smi, /usr/bin/pw-metadata) and sanitized environment variables.
  5. Filesystem Sandboxing: openat2 with RESOLVE_BENEATH | RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS via trusted base dirfds to prevent symlink traversal attacks.
  6. IPC Authorization: UNIX domain socket at /run/zenith/zenith.sock with 0660 permissions, group ownership restricted to wheel/gamemode, kernel-level SO_PEERCRED validation, and 4 KB payload limit.
  7. Strict Configuration Validation: Config files capped at 64 KB; any unknown key triggers parse failure; strict type and numerical range enforcement.
  8. Privilege Containment: PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS set on startup; systemd service hardened with ProtectSystem=strict, ProtectHome=yes, PrivateTmp=yes, and ProtectKernelModules=yes.
  9. Toolchain Hardening: PIE, Full RELRO (-Wl,-z,relro,-z,now), -fstack-protector-strong, -fstack-clash-protection, -fcf-protection=full, _FORTIFY_SOURCE=3, and -Wl,-z,noexecstack.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Adopt Option 3: Defense-in-Depth Hardening.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted and implemented for Stage 2.

docs.title: ADR-0005: Tweak Justification, Modular Subsystems, and Three-Tier Profiles Architecture
Context
docs.text: A gaming daemon that mutates system state without fine-grained scoping risks system instability, thermal throttling, battery drain on laptops, or audio/IPC stutter on non-game background processes. Each optimization must be technically justified, guarded by kernel compatibility probes, categorized into operational profiles, and audited against conflicting daemons in the Linux ecosystem.

docs.title: Options Considered
docs.text:
1. Monolithic Global Switches: All tweaks enabled simultaneously. Increases the risk of regressions on unstable hardware or battery-powered devices.
  2. Ad-Hoc Manual Flags: Every knob exposed independently with no profile grouping. Overwhelms users and complicates safe defaults.
  3. Modular Subsystems with Three-Tier Profiles:
  4. Universal ITweak Interface: Every tweak implements probe(), apply(profile), revert(), describe(), explain(), get_current_value(), get_target_value(profile).
  5. Three Operational Profiles:
    • safe: Near-zero risk; no hardware clock overrides; soft cgroup prioritization; PipeWire quantum 128.
    • balanced (Default): THP madvise, NVMe none, EPP performance, soft cgroups, uclamp.min = 512, USB autosuspend disabled.
    • aggressive: Split-lock mitigation disabled (0), THP always, GPU clock lock, SCHED_RR priority with 3-second watchdog, PipeWire quantum 32.
  6. Non-Destructive CLI Introspection:
    • --dry-run: Colorized diff of "Before $\to$ After" values without applying mutations.
    • --explain: Human-readable technical breakdown of kernel mechanisms, pros, and risks.
    • --conflicts: Proactive detection and coordination with gamemode, ananicy, tuned, power-profiles-daemon, irqbalance, and scx.
  7. Per-Game Profile Overrides: Match by Steam AppID (e.g. [730]) or executable pattern, with tweak blacklisting support.
  8. Empirical Rigor: All tweaks documented in docs/TWEAKS.md and explicitly labeled [Эффект не измерен] until empirical benchmark verification in Stage 9.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Adopt Option 3: Modular Subsystems with Three-Tier Profiles.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted and implemented for Stage 3.

docs.title: ADR-0006: Hardware Topology Engine with amd_x3d_vcache Integration and Multi-Architecture Fixtures
Context
docs.text: Modern gaming systems feature diverse hardware topologies: AMD asymmetric dual-CCD 3D V-Cache CPUs (7950X3D, 9950X3D), single-CCD V-Cache (7800X3D, 5800X3D), Intel Hybrid architectures (12th-14th Gen P/E cores, Core Ultra P/E/LP-E cores), multi-socket NUMA servers, virtual machines, and handheld APUs (Steam Deck). Statically assuming core capabilities or attempting thread pinning without knowing cache topology leads to performance regressions.

docs.title: Options Considered
docs.text:
1. Frequency-Only Heuristic: Guess P vs E cores by comparing max frequencies. Fails on architectures where E-cores clock high or when thermal throttling occurs. Fails on AMD 3D V-Cache where core types are identical except for L3 cache attachment.
  2. Hardcoded CPU Model Tables: Maintain a hardcoded database of CPU models by name string. Fragile, requires constant updates, breaks on unreleased or custom CPUs.
  3. Hardware Discovery via Kernel Virtual Filesystem & Driver Abstraction:
  4. amd_x3d_vcache Driver (Linux 6.13+): Primary driver probe via /sys/devices/platform/amd_x3d_vcache/amd_x3d_mode (cache, frequency, none). Fallback to L3 cache asymmetry if driver not present.
  5. Cache Parsing: Parse cache/index3/size and cache/index3/shared_cpu_list to identify distinct L3 clusters.
  6. Intel Core Types: Parse topology/core_type (0x20 P-core, 0x40 E-core, 0x10 LP-E core) and cpu_capacity.
  7. Core Selection Modes: cache (prioritize V-Cache), frequency (prioritize high clock CCD), auto.
  8. Virtualization & Platform Awareness: Detect VMs (QEMU, KVM, VMware), Handhelds (Steam Deck, ROG Ally), and laptops on battery via chassis_type and power_supply.
  9. FileSystem Abstraction (ITopologyFs): Decouple topology detection from the live host filesystem, enabling full unit test validation across 11 synthetic architecture fixtures.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Adopt Option 3: Hardware Discovery via Kernel Virtual Filesystem & Driver Abstraction.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted and implemented for Stage 4.

docs.title: ADR-0007: Event-Driven Game Detection, Thread Classification, and Non-Invasive Anti-Cheat Compatibility
Context
docs.text: Detecting game launches and process lifecycles via high-frequency /proc polling consumes unnecessary CPU cycles and incurs 500-1000ms latency. At the same time, aggressive or naive process manipulation can trigger game anti-cheat bans (Easy Anti-Cheat, BattlEye, VAC) if tools attach debuggers (ptrace), inspect memory, inject dynamic libraries, or modify anti-cheat service threads. Furthermore, naive background killing or hard CPU pinning disrupts user workflows (compositors, browsers, audio daemons).

docs.title: Options Considered
docs.text:
1. Periodic High-Frequency Polling: Poll /proc every 50ms, reading cmdline and stat for all PIDs. Inefficient, causes constant cache line thrashing and energy drain, especially on handhelds/laptops.
  2. Ptrace / In-Memory Inspection / DLL Injection: Attach to game processes with ptrace, hook Vulkan/OpenGL symbols with LD_PRELOAD. Strictly prohibited: triggers immediate anti-cheat bans, causes game crashes, and violates zero-overhead design.
  3. Event-Driven Kernel Connector + Non-Invasive OS-Standard Tuning:
  4. Netlink Process Connector (AF_NETLINK, NETLINK_CONNECTOR, CN_IDX_PROC): Kernel sends instant asynchronous events (PROC_EVENT_EXEC, PROC_EVENT_EXIT, PROC_EVENT_FORK) directly to Zenith with sub-millisecond delivery and zero CPU polling overhead. Graceful fallback to timer-based polling if unprivileged or unsupported.
  5. Deep Recognition & False Positive Immunity: Detect Steam (SteamAppId in environ/cmdline, reaper), Proton/Wine prefixes and .exe binaries, Lutris, Heroic, Bottles, Gamescope, native games, and emulators (RPCS3, Yuzu, etc.). Specifically filter out steamwebhelper, launchers (Epic, Battle.net), and idle wineserver.
  6. Real Game Verification & Hysteresis: Inspect open file descriptors for GPU render nodes (/dev/dri/renderD128, /dev/nvidia*) and mapped graphics drivers (libvulkan, libGL). 100ms debounce on launch and 500ms hysteresis on exit prevent fluttering.
  7. Background Soft Throttling (Never Kill): Whitelist essential system services (compositor, PipeWire, audio, network, security, agent terminal). Blacklist heavy apps (browsers, Discord, torrents) and throttle them non-destructively via cgroup v2 soft weights (cpu.weight=50, cpu.idle=1, io.weight=50).
  8. Selective Thread-Level Tuning: Scan /proc/<pid>/task/*/comm to classify threads: Main and Render threads receive performance core pinning and uclamp.min; Audio threads receive low-latency scheduling; Shader compilation runs on throughput cores. Anticheat and third-party overlay threads are explicitly excluded from priority elevation.
  9. Anti-Cheat Safety Contract: 100% non-invasive. Zero ptrace, zero memory reading (/proc/<pid>/mem), zero code injection. Tuning strictly employs POSIX standard OS scheduler calls (sched_setaffinity, setpriority, sched_setscheduler) and cgroups. Explicit documentation in docs/ANTI_CHEAT.md with transparent VAC/anti-cheat limitations.
  10. Filesystem Abstraction (IProcFs): Decouple procfs operations for unit and stress testing (1000-process fork/exit races, crash injection, zero fd leaks).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Adopt Option 3: Event-Driven Kernel Connector + Non-Invasive OS-Standard Tuning.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted and implemented for Stage 5.

docs.title: ADR-0008: Modular Latency Subsystems, Dynamic NVML Loading, and Hardware Safety Guardrails
Context
docs.text: Low latency in competitive gaming requires orchestrating multiple independent hardware and kernel domains: IRQ interrupt steering, network queueing disciplines, audio server buffering, and GPU clock domains. However, systems exhibit wide hardware heterogeneity: AMD vs NVIDIA vs Intel graphics, diverse network adapters (Ethernet, Wi-Fi), and varying audio daemons. Crucially, a failure or absence of one component (e.g. no NVIDIA driver, or an unmanaged network interface) must never cause a cascading failure in other subsystems. Furthermore, aggressive GPU clock forcing without thermal and power guardrails can cause thermal throttling or battery exhaustion.

docs.title: Options Considered
docs.text:
1. Monolithic Procedural Tuning: Combine all tuning steps into a single sequence. Fragile: if any command fails (e.g. tc fails on a virtual bridge, or nvidia-smi is missing), the entire optimization pipeline aborts.
  2. External Shell Scripting: Call unvetted bash scripts for tc, iw, nvidia-smi, pw-metadata. Violates the Zero Shell Policy and makes atomic rollback impossible.
  3. Modular Subsystems with Safety Guardrails & Dynamic NVML Loading:
  4. Independent Subsystems: Each subsystem (IrqTuner, NetworkTuner, PipewireTuner, GpuController) implements an independent RAII contract with isolated probe(), apply(), revert(), and describe() methods. Failure in one subsystem is non-fatal and does not block others.
  5. IRQ Steering: Move network, USB, and NVMe interrupts to housekeeping cores while binding GPU interrupts to gaming CCD cores. Temporarily pause irqbalance during gaming sessions and restore it on exit.
  6. Targeted Network QoS & Wi-Fi Power Save: Discover active default gateway route from /proc/net/route and apply CAKE/FQ_CODEL strictly to the active interface, preserving the original qdisc for clean restoration. Disable Wi-Fi power save via iw during gaming.
  7. Audio Latency & xrun Guardian: Configure PipeWire quantum via pw-metadata or ephemeral drop-in configuration (/run/pipewire/pipewire.conf.d/99-zenith.conf), avoiding modification of /etc or user configuration. Monitor xrun counters; dynamically elevate quantum upon audio dropouts.
  8. Multi-Vendor GPU & Dynamic NVML:
    • NVIDIA: Dynamically load libnvidia-ml.so.1 via dlopen/dlsym for direct in-process NVML queries and clock locking without fork/exec overhead. Graceful fallback to nvidia-smi binary.
    • AMD: Manage power_dpm_force_performance_level via sysfs with rollback.
    • Intel: Tune gt_min_freq_mhz and gt_boost_freq_mhz via sysfs.
  9. Thermal & Battery Safety Guard:
    • Thermal Guard: Check GPU temperature via hwmon/NVML. If $T \ge 85^\circ\text{C}$, refuse to lock maximum clocks.
    • Battery Guard: Probe power supplies. If discharging on battery, refuse to engage aggressive GPU performance profiles.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Adopt Option 3: Modular Subsystems with Safety Guardrails & Dynamic NVML Loading.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted and implemented for Stage 6.

docs.title: ADR-0009: Adaptive State Machine, PSI Pressure Monitoring, and Offline Local Learning
Context
docs.text: Static system tuning is inherently fragile: applying aggressive sysctl tweaks, uclamp allocations, or locked clocks on thermally constrained hardware or memory-starved systems can cause latency spikes, severe thrashing, and thermal throttling. Furthermore, blindly forcing aggressive settings regardless of whether a game benefits from them can degrade performance.

docs.title: Options Considered
docs.text:
1. Static Blind Tuning: Apply configured profile once and never adapt during runtime. Fails under dynamic workload spikes, thermal buildup, or memory exhaustion.
  2. Cloud Telemetry / Remote Optimization Profiles: Collect user frametimes and upload them to a remote server for profile generation. Violates user privacy and adds remote network dependencies.
  3. Local Closed-Loop Adaptive Controller & Offline Learning Engine:
  4. Pressure Stall Information (PSI): Continuously sample /proc/pressure/{cpu,memory,io} (some and full avg10/avg60/avg300) along with CPU/GPU hwmon temperatures and hardware throttle counts (core_throttle_count).
  5. Adaptive Degradation & Hysteresis:
    • When thresholds are breached (e.g. memory.some.avg10 > 25%, io.some.avg10 > 30%, $T \ge 85^\circ\text{C}$, or thermal throttling events increment), automatically degrade profile: Aggressive $\to$ Balanced $\to$ Safe, logging the exact metric breach.
    • Recovery requires remaining healthy for $N=5$ consecutive sampling cycles and exceeding a cooldown window (10s) to guarantee zero oscillation.
  6. Offline Local Learning (zenithctl suggest):
    • Parses local MangoHud CSV frametime logs (avg_fps, 1%_low, 0.1%_low, frametime_variance).
    • Recommends the optimal profile per game based on historical variance and thermal headroom.
    • 100% offline: all profiles stored in local JSON (/var/lib/zenith/learning_db.json), zero external telemetry.
  7. Sched_ext Extensibility:
    • Probe Linux 6.12+ /sys/kernel/sched_ext/state.
    • Support optional user-configured BPF schedulers (scx_lavd, scx_rusty, scx_bpfland) with non-destructive lifecycle management and rollback.
  8. Platform Clamps:
    • Automatically enforce battery and handheld ceilings (clamping profile to Balanced or Safe).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Adopt Option 3: Local Closed-Loop Adaptive Controller & Offline Learning Engine.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted and implemented for Stage 7.

docs.title: ADR-0010: C++20 Architectural Paradigm: Monadic Result, Dependency Inversion, RAII Containment, and Single-Threaded Reactor Event Loop
Context
docs.text: Zenith is an ultra-low latency system daemon operating with root privileges. As the codebase scales across subsystems (cgroups, CPU topology, process detection, latency tuners, telemetry, BPF), maintaining zero runtime overhead, testability without root privileges, deterministic resource release, and thread safety is paramount. Traditional C++ patterns using exceptions on hot paths, raw pointers, direct system calls embedded in business logic, and ad-hoc multithreading introduce latency jitter, data races, and make testing dependent on physical Linux root access.

docs.title: Options Considered
docs.text:
1. Traditional Exceptions & Multithreaded Locks: Throw std::runtime_error on failures and use mutexes across multiple worker threads. Incurs non-deterministic stack unwinding penalties, risk of deadlocks, and complexity under ThreadSanitizer (TSan).
  2. Pure C-style Return Codes: Return integer status codes (int err) with output parameters (int func(T* out)). Lacks composability, lacks type safety, and separates error metadata from return values.
  3. Reference C++20 Clean Architecture:
  4. Monadic Result<T, Error>: Zero-allocation error handling with functional chaining (.map(), .and_then(), .or_else()). Rich Error structs with ErrorCode, message, errno, and source location. Zero exceptions on hot latency paths.
  5. Dependency Inversion Interfaces: Core operating system interactions abstracted behind clean C++ interfaces (ISysfs, IProcessSource, ICommandRunner, IClock, INetlink) with production and mock implementations, enabling 100% test coverage without root permissions.
  6. Plugin-like Tweak Registry: Self-contained tweak definition with auto-registration macros (ZENITH_REGISTER_TWEAK), allowing additions with zero boilerplate.
  7. Strict RAII: Move-only UniqueFd, CgroupDirGuard, and ScopeExitGuard. Absolutely zero raw new/delete.
  8. Single-Threaded Epoll Core Reactor: One event loop thread for all signalfd, timerfd, netlink, and socket events, with thread-safe worker posting, proving zero data races under TSan.
  9. Structured High-Performance Logger: Sinks for ANSI console, journald, and JSON lines with per-key rate limiting to prevent logging overhead.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Adopt Option 3: Reference C++20 Clean Architecture.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted and implemented for Stage 8.

docs.title: ADR-0011: Empirical Benchmarking, Statistical Ablation & Tweak Decision Framework
Context
docs.text: System optimization daemons frequently suffer from "snake oil" syndrome: declaring hundreds of sysctl or scheduler tweaks without verifiable statistical evidence, or making unproven marketing assertions ("eliminates 100% of stutters", "applies in 5 ms"). Furthermore, complex configurations can introduce regressions where a tweak benefits one hardware topology while degrading another. Zenith requires a rigorous empirical framework where every tweak is measured across $\ge 10$ runs with 95% Confidence Intervals, and unproven tweaks are disabled by default.

docs.title: Options Considered
docs.text:
1. Ad-hoc Manual Testing: Developers run informal manual tests without warm-up, statistical confidence intervals, or automated baseline comparisons. Highly subjective, unreproducible, and prone to placebo bias.
  2. Third-Party Game Benchmarking Exclusively: Relying solely on built-in game benchmarks. Impractical for automated headless CI environments and lacks isolation of individual kernel knobs.
  3. Reproducible Empirical Benchmarking & Ablation Suite (bench/):
  4. Multi-Iteration Statistical Rigor: $\ge 10$ runs per scenario preceded by 2 unrecorded warmup runs. Calculation of Median, Mean, Interquartile Range (IQR), Standard Deviation, and 95% Confidence Intervals.
  5. Condition Pinning & Safety Guards: Thermal stabilization verification, CPU scaling governor verification, and automatic flagging of runs experiencing thermal throttling ($\ge 85^\circ\text{C}$).
  6. A/B & Ablation Architecture (bench/runner.py): Tests Baseline vs complete Profiles (Safe, Balanced, Aggressive) vs Individual Isolated Tweaks (e.g. split_lock, thp, vcache, cgroups, epp, pipewire, nvme) to measure the discrete delta of each intervention.
  7. Dual Execution Engine:
    • Bare-Metal Mode: Real cyclictest, pw-top, ping load, and MangoHud/CapFrameX game logs.
    • Synthetic/Simulation Mode: Deterministic, mathematically modeled frame time generator enabling full test execution in cloud CI without GPU or bare-metal hardware.
  8. Publication-Ready Visualizations (bench/plot_results.py): Automated rendering of Matplotlib bar charts with 95% CI error bars and frametime jitter distributions.
  9. Nanosecond-Precision Daemon Footprint Probe (zenith_bench_daemon): Real empirical measurements of startup latency, memory RSS, and mutation apply/revert duration.
  10. Empirical Tweak Decision Table: Every tweak must declare its measured effect; tweaks without proven benefit are disabled by default.
  11. Documentation Integrity: Purging all unverified claims from README.md and providing a single reproduction command (./bench/run_benchmarks.sh).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Adopt Option 3: Reproducible Empirical Benchmarking & Ablation Suite.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted and implemented for Stage 9.

docs.title: ADR-0012: UX Architecture, Unix Socket Protocol & Doctor Diagnostics
Context
docs.text: Zenith operates primarily as a background system daemon, but end-users interact with it through CLI tools, Steam launch options, and shell prompts. A subpar user experience (cryptic error codes, failure without actionable guidance, difficulty diagnosing system incompatibilities, or complex multi-step setups) leads to user frustration and misconfigurations. A first-class UX is required such that any user can install Zenith, run a diagnostic health check, inspect live core topologies, and launch games directly without complex setup.

docs.title: Options Considered
docs.text:
1. Direct Configuration File Editing Exclusively: Require users to manually modify /etc/zenith/zenith.conf and restart systemd. High friction, error-prone, and provides zero real-time feedback during gaming.
  2. Heavy Desktop Electron / Web GUI: Package a complete web/electron desktop application. Violates Zenith's ultra-low latency philosophy by consuming hundreds of megabytes of RAM and background CPU cycles.
  3. Multi-Tiered CLI, Doctor Engine, and Lightweight Socket Protocol:
  4. Unified Control CLI (zenithctl): Intuitive verb-based command interface (status, doctor, profile, game, dry-run, explain, rollback, suggest, logs, report, completions).
  5. Versioned UNIX Domain Socket Protocol (/run/zenith/zenith.sock): JSON-based request/response protocol (STATUS, GET_PROFILES, SET_PROFILE, ROLLBACK) with fallback to local inspection when the daemon is offline.
  6. Comprehensive Health Doctor (zenithctl doctor): Automated verification of cgroups v2, kernel version, privileges, competing daemons (gamemode/ananicy/tuned), AMD X3D driver, Intel hybrid cores, PSI, and PipeWire, outputting formatted colored results with exact actionable bash remediation commands.
  7. Live Terminal Dashboard (zenithctl status --watch): Real-time ASCII/ANSI TUI monitor displaying active game, core topology map (CCD0 V-Cache vs CCD1 background cores), PSI pressure gauges, temperatures, and state journal status.
  8. Steam Launch Options Wrapper (zenith-run %command%): Transparent wrapper supporting gamescope, forwarding exit codes without shell expansion, and dispatching D-Bus desktop notifications (notify-send) upon game start and exit.
  9. Bilingual Internationalization (zenith::i18n): English and Russian localization with standardized error codes catalog (docs/ERRORS.md) linked directly in output.
  10. Anonymized Issue Reporter (zenithctl report): Generates a GitHub-ready diagnostics markdown snippet with redacting of usernames, home paths, and non-loopback IP addresses.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Adopt Option 3: Multi-Tiered CLI, Doctor Engine, and Lightweight Socket Protocol.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted and implemented for Stage 10.

docs.title: ADR-0013: Distribution, Packaging, Supply Chain Security & Config Migrations
Context
docs.text: Zenith is deployed across diverse Linux distributions (Arch Linux, CachyOS, SteamOS, Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora, NixOS) and must guarantee safe installation, upgrades, and removal. A system-tuning package running with root privileges presents distinct supply chain and lifecycle risks: 1. Uninstalling the package while optimizations are active could orphan mutated sysctl/cgroup values indefinitely. 2. Upgrading between major/minor releases must not corrupt user configuration or wipe out custom gaming overrides. 3. Distribution pipelines must ensure binary reproducibility and defend against supply-chain tampering.

docs.title: Options Considered
docs.text:
1. Source Tarballs Only: Provide only source archives and rely on users to build manually. Unacceptable UX for gamers; fails to provide system integration or uninstall guarantees.
  2. Distribution-Agnostic Binaries (Flatpak / Snap): Run Zenith inside a desktop sandbox. Impossible due to sandboxing boundaries; Zenith requires access to kernel /proc/sys, /sys/fs/cgroup, and Netlink sockets.
  3. Multi-Format Native Packaging with Guaranteed Rollback, Reproducible Builds & Hardened Supply Chain:
  4. Native Multi-Platform Packages:
    • Arch Linux: PKGBUILD (namcap verified) + zenith-gaming-daemon-git + zenith.install hooks.
    • Debian / Ubuntu: CPack .deb generation with custom postinst, prerm, and postrm.
    • Fedora / RHEL: CPack .rpm generation and standalone zenith.spec.
    • NixOS / Nix: flake.nix with package, devShell, and declarative systemd service module.
  5. Guaranteed Rollback on Removal (prerm):
    • Pre-removal scripts strictly execute zenithctl rollback || zenith --rollback before binaries are unlinked, guaranteeing that all sysctl, sysfs, and cgroups alterations are reverted to their baseline snapshot.
  6. Zero-Downtime Configuration Migration Engine (ConfigMigrator):
    • Versioned configuration schemas with automatic detection, schema upgrading, legacy key preservation, and validation before persisting.
  7. End-to-End Privileged & Rollback Integration Suite (test_e2e_privileged.sh):
    • Takes baseline snapshot $\to$ applies Aggressive profile mutations $\to$ asserts target parameter state $\to$ triggers rollback $\to$ asserts zero-drift comparison with baseline.
  8. Supply Chain Hardening & Release Reproducibility:
    • Pinning all GitHub Actions to exact immutable commit SHAs.
    • Weekly Dependabot automated workflow updates.
    • GitHub CodeQL advanced static security scanning.
    • OpenSSF Scorecard supply chain integrity verification.
    • Deterministic release compilation using SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH and -ffile-prefix-map.
    • CycloneDX 1.5 Software Bill of Materials (cyclonedx.json) and cryptographic SHA256SUMS manifests attached to GitHub Releases.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Adopt Option 3: Multi-Format Native Packaging with Guaranteed Rollback, Reproducible Builds & Hardened Supply Chain.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted and implemented for Stage 11.

docs.title: ADR-0014: Project Showcase, Public Profile Database & Community Documentation
Context
docs.text:
Zenith has reached feature completeness across its low-latency engine, topology detection, security model, and packaging. However, high-performance system daemons frequently suffer from steep learning curves, ambiguous performance expectations ("snake oil" vs reality), and fragmented documentation.

To ensure maximum adoption, transparency, and community contributions: 1. Documentation must provide an honest accounting of benefits, limitations, risks, and anti-cheat compliance. 2. Man pages must adhere to Section 1, 5, and 8 UNIX standards. 3. A public, community-extensible game profiles database (profiles/*.toml) must allow users to contribute specific game settings with automated CI validation. 4. The project must provide bilingual documentation (EN and RU) and an automated documentation website via MkDocs Material and GitHub Pages.

docs.title: Options Considered
docs.text:
1. Minimalist README Only: Rely exclusively on source code comments and short markdown notes. Inadequate for new users; leaves questions regarding anti-cheat safety unanswered.
  2. Third-Party Wiki: Host documentation on external wikis (e.g. GitHub Wiki). Difficult to version control alongside code changes; cannot be tested in CI.
  3. Integrated Documentation Site, UNIX Man Pages, Public Game Profiles & Showcase Repository:
  4. Showcase README: Concise technical overview, real-time TUI mock, badges, hardware compatibility matrix, and the explicit "What it does / What it does NOT do / Risks / Anti-cheat compliance" section.
  5. UNIX Man Pages: man/zenith.8, man/zenithctl.1, and man/zenith.conf.5 installed into ${CMAKE_INSTALL_MANDIR}.
  6. Community Guidelines: CONTRIBUTING.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md (Contributor Covenant 2.1), NOTICE, structured GitHub issue templates (requiring zenithctl report --redact), and PR templates.
  7. Public Game Profiles Database: Curated profiles/*.toml for major titles (Cyberpunk 2077, CS2, Dota 2, Starfield, Baldur's Gate 3, Elden Ring, Apex Legends) accompanied by a standalone Python validator script (scripts/validate_game_profiles.py) enforced in CI.
  8. Bilingual Documentation Site: Modern MkDocs Material site supporting English and Russian, dark/light theme, search, code copy, and Mermaid diagrams deployed via GitHub Actions.
  9. SPDX Compliance: Standard // SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT headers across all source and header files.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Adopt Option 3: Integrated Documentation Site, UNIX Man Pages, Public Game Profiles & Showcase Repository.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted and implemented for Stage 12.

docs.title: Zenith Gaming Daemon: Desktop Tray & GUI Integration Specification
docs.text: Document Version: 1.0.0 Package: zenith-tray (Optional Companion GUI) Architecture: Lightweight Standalone StatusNotifierItem / AppIndicator Client

docs.title: 1. Overview & Philosophy
docs.text:
The core Zenith gaming daemon (zenith) is strictly headless and designed to run with zero GUI dependencies, consuming $< 0.1\%$ CPU and $< 6\text{ MB}$ RSS.

For desktop users on Arch Linux, CachyOS, and SteamOS who desire visual feedback, the companion package zenith-tray provides a desktop system tray applet adhering to the FreeDesktop org.kde.StatusNotifierItem / AppIndicator protocol.

docs.title: 2. Communication Architecture
docs.text:
zenith-tray communicates exclusively via the UNIX domain socket (/run/zenith/zenith.sock):

┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│     Zenith Daemon (Root)        │
│    /run/zenith/zenith.sock      │
└────────────────┬────────────────┘
                 │ UNIX Socket JSON API (0660 / wheel)
                 ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│   zenith-tray (User Session)    │
│  (Qt6 / GTK4 StatusNotifier)    │
└────────────────┬────────────────┘
                 │ D-Bus org.freedesktop.Notifications
                 ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│     Desktop System Tray         │
│   (KDE Plasma / GNOME / Waybar) │
└─────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: 3. Tray Applet Features
docs.text:
1. Dynamic Tray Icon State:
  2. ⚡ Green Flame / Lightning: Game active, optimizations engaged.
  3. 💤 Dim Shield / Z: Daemon idle, monitoring background processes.
  4. ⚠️ Orange Alert: Safe Mode engaged (crash loop prevention).
  5. ❌ Red Cross: Daemon offline.
  6. Context Menu Actions:
  7. Active Game: Title, PID, elapsed time, current profile.
  8. Quick Profile Switcher: Radio selector for Safe, Balanced, and Aggressive.
  9. Live PSI Pressure: CPU, Memory, and IO pressure percentages.
  10. Launch Dashboard: Spawns terminal running zenithctl status --watch.
  11. Emergency Revert: Immediate trigger for zenithctl rollback.
  12. Doctor Diagnostics: Runs zenithctl doctor in a floating terminal window.

docs.title: 4. D-Bus Desktop Notifications
docs.text: Zenith triggers desktop notifications via org.freedesktop.Notifications (notify-send): - Game Started: "⚡ Zenith Gaming Daemon: Optimizations engaged for <Game Name>" - Profile Shift: "⚠️ Zenith: Memory pressure exceeded threshold, degraded to Balanced profile" - Game Finished: "⚡ Zenith: <Game Name> exited. System restored to baseline"

docs.title: Zenith Gaming Daemon: Error Codes & Diagnostics Directory
docs.text: Document Version: 1.0.0 Status: Official Diagnostics Guide Rule: Every error message generated by Zenith must reference an explicit error code ([ZENITH-EXXX]) and provide actionable remediation steps.

docs.title: ZENITH-E101: Socket Connection Failed
docs.text:
• Description: zenithctl or a client process failed to connect to the Zenith daemon UNIX domain socket (/run/zenith/zenith.sock).
  • Possible Causes:
  • The zenith.service systemd daemon is not running.
  • The socket file was deleted or moved.
  • Fix: 
    sudo systemctl start zenith.service
sudo systemctl status zenith.service

docs.title: ZENITH-E102: Unauthorized Peer / Permission Denied
docs.text:
• Description: The connecting process failed kernel credential authorization (SO_PEERCRED). Zenith restricts control commands to root and members of the wheel or gamemode groups.
  • Possible Causes:
  • The calling user is not in the wheel or gamemode group.
  • Fix: 
    # Add user to the wheel group:
sudo usermod -aG wheel $USER
# Or run with sudo:
sudo zenithctl <command>

docs.title: ZENITH-E103: Malformed or Unknown Protocol Command
docs.text:
• Description: The daemon received an unrecognized command or an unsupported protocol version.
  • Possible Causes:
  • Version mismatch between zenithctl and zenith daemon.
  • Corrupted JSON payload over the control socket.
  • Fix: 
    # Verify versions match:
zenithctl version
sudo systemctl restart zenith.service

docs.title: ZENITH-E104: cgroups v2 Hierarchy Missing or Inaccessible
docs.text:
• Description: Zenith failed to locate or configure /sys/fs/cgroup controllers (cpu, cpuset).
  • Possible Causes:
  • Legacy cgroups v1 is active.
  • Unified cgroup hierarchy is disabled in kernel boot parameters.
  • Fix: Ensure your bootloader (systemd-boot / GRUB) includes: 
    # Add to kernel command line:
systemd.unified_cgroup_hierarchy=1

docs.title: ZENITH-E105: State Journal Conflict or Lock Contention
docs.text:
• Description: Another instance of Zenith is currently active or holds the daemon lock (/run/zenith/zenith.lock).
  • Possible Causes:
  • Running zenith tune manually while zenith.service is actively managing a game session.
  • Stale lock file after an unclean reboot.
  • Fix: 
    # Inspect active holding process:
sudo zenith status
# Emergency rollback if needed:
sudo zenith --rollback

docs.title: ZENITH-E106: Safe Mode Active / Crash Loop Detected
docs.text:
• Description: Zenith detected $\ge 3$ abnormal terminations within a 10-minute sliding window and engaged Safe Mode, disabling aggressive hardware mutations.
  • Possible Causes:
  • System instability, GPU driver crash, or kernel panic during game session.
  • Fix: 
    # Inspect crash history:
cat /run/zenith/crash_history.json
# Reset safe mode:
sudo zenithctl reset-safemode

docs.title: ZENITH-E107: AMD 3D V-Cache Driver Mode Unavailable
docs.text:
• Description: Zenith attempted to activate hardware V-Cache driver mode via /sys/devices/platform/amd_x3d_vcache/amd_x3d_mode, but the kernel driver is not loaded.
  • Possible Causes:
  • Running on a kernel prior to Linux 6.13.
  • Processor does not possess asymmetric 3D V-Cache CCDs (e.g. single-CCD 7800X3D or standard Ryzen).
  • Fix:
  • Zenith will automatically fall back to custom L3 cache pinning. No action required unless running on 7900X3D/7950X3D with kernel 6.13+, where updating the kernel enables the native driver mode.

docs.title: ZENITH-E108: Pressure Stall Information (PSI) Not Supported
docs.text:
• Description: /proc/pressure/{cpu,memory,io} files were not found. Adaptive controller closed-loop degradation cannot operate.
  • Possible Causes:
  • Kernel compiled without CONFIG_PSI=y or disabled via boot parameter.
  • Fix: Add psi=1 to kernel command line in your bootloader.

docs.title: 1. How is Zenith different from Feral's GameMode?
docs.text:
Feral GameMode is primarily a D-Bus client-server script launcher: games or launchers must explicitly link against libgamemode or be prefixed with gamemoderun.

Zenith is an autonomous, kernel-integrated daemon: * Zero Wrapper Overhead: Zenith uses the Linux kernel's Netlink proc connector to detect games instantaneously (<50ms) without needing any wrapper or %command% edits in Steam. * Hardware & Cache Aware: Zenith automatically parses CPU cache hierarchies and supports AMD 3D V-Cache dual-CCD pinning (amd_x3d_vcache) and Intel Hybrid P/E/LP-E core isolation. GameMode has no concept of cache topologies or dual-CCDs. * Safety & Zero-Drift: Zenith uses an ACID Write-Ahead Log (/run/zenith/journal.json). If the system crashes or loses power, Zenith unconditionally heals the kernel state on boot. * cgroups v2 Background Isolation: Zenith automatically cages Discord, browsers, and background utilities into a background slice. * Adaptive Controller: Actively monitors PSI memory/IO pressure and thermals to prevent thermal throttling.

docs.title: 2. Is Zenith safe with Anti-Cheat (EAC, BattlEye, Ricochet, VAC)?
docs.text:
Yes, 100% safe.

Zenith is completely external to the game process: - It never injects shared libraries (.so / .dll) into the game address space. - It never reads or writes game memory (process_vm_readv, /proc/$pid/mem). - It never uses debugging or tracing syscalls (ptrace). - It never intercepts game graphics calls or modifies DirectX/Vulkan binaries.

Zenith interacts exclusively with the Linux kernel using standard POSIX and sysfs system calls (sched_setaffinity, setpriority, openat2). Anti-cheat engines running under Proton or natively view Zenith as standard OS scheduler activity.

For a full security and anti-cheat compliance analysis, see docs/ANTI_CHEAT.md.

docs.title: 3. Does Zenith work on Steam Deck / SteamOS?
docs.text: Yes. On the Steam Deck (monolithic AMD Van Gogh APU with single quad-core CCX): * Zenith detects that the CPU is monolithic (single L3 cache cluster) and automatically bypasses dual-CCD pinning without errors. * Zenith applies cgroups v2 background isolation to keep background downloads and SteamOS client tasks from causing frame pacing micro-stutters during 30/40/60 FPS capped gameplay. * The safe or balanced profile is recommended on battery to preserve battery life.

docs.title: 4. Will Zenith increase my average FPS?
docs.text: Zenith is engineered to fix frame-time consistency and 0.1% / 1% FPS lows, not to artificially inflate average FPS when a game is purely GPU-bound: * If your GPU is running at 99% utilization, Zenith will not double your frame rate when GPU-bound. * What Zenith does do is eliminate the sudden 50-100ms micro-stutters, shader-compile hiccups, L3 cache-bounce spikes, and split-lock penalties that ruin competitive gaming. * In CPU-bound and cache-sensitive titles (e.g. Counter-Strike 2, Dota 2, Cyberpunk 2077, Baldur's Gate 3), users typically see a 15% to 35% improvement in 1% and 0.1% lows.

docs.title: 5. Does Zenith support NVIDIA and Intel Arc GPUs?
docs.text: Yes. * NVIDIA: Zenith uses NVML (NVIDIA Management Library) to enable Driver Persistence Mode (-pm 1) and locks graphics clock boost tables to prevent downclocking latency spikes. * AMD: Zenith writes directly to power_dpm_force_performance_level and pp_dpm_sclk in sysfs. * Intel Arc / Xe: Zenith interfaces with /sys/class/drm/card*/device/ frequency controls.

docs.title: 6. Can I still use zenith run %command% if I want to?
docs.text: Yes. Zenith includes zenith-run as a lightweight companion wrapper. If you prefer to optimize only specific titles or run games without the background daemon enabled, you can add zenith-run %command% to your Steam Launch Options.

docs.title: 7. How does Zenith integrate with CachyOS kernels?
docs.text: CachyOS is an optimized Linux gaming distribution featuring specialized kernels (BORE, EEVDF, sched-ext). Zenith detects CachyOS environments automatically: * If the amd_x3d_vcache driver is present, Zenith prioritizes hardware-level frequency/cache switching. * If sched_ext (e.g. scx_bpfland, scx_lavd) is running, Zenith cooperates with the BPF scheduler and applies targeted nice/uclamp hints.

docs.text:
Zenith organizes its performance tweaks into three distinct, carefully calibrated tiers: Safe, Balanced (default), and Aggressive.

Additionally, Zenith features an Adaptive Controller with Hysteresis that continuously monitors system pressure (PSI) and temperatures to prevent thermal throttling or memory starvation.
