docs.title: 1. Safe Profile (safe)
docs.text:
• Philosophy: Conservative baseline. Standard power draw and thermal limits.
  • Intended Audience: Handhelds on battery power (Steam Deck, ROG Ally), laptops, enterprise developer workstations, systems with marginal cooling.
  • Mechanism: Binds game threads strictly through CPU affinity (CCD0 or P-cores) and moves browser/Discord background processes to core 0 via cgroups v2. Leaves all sysctl, memory, and GPU power domains completely untouched.

docs.title: 2. Balanced Profile (balanced - Default)
docs.text:
• Philosophy: Standard desktop profile. Balances frame pacing with system stability and energy efficiency.
  • Intended Audience: Modern desktop gaming rigs (AMD Ryzen 5000/7000/9000, Intel 12th-14th Gen, Core Ultra).
  • Mechanism:
  • Engages full 3D V-Cache / P-Core affinity pinning.
  • Modulates virtual memory parameters (vm.swappiness=10, vm.dirty_ratio=5, vm.compaction_proactiveness=0) to eliminate background IO hitching.
  • Lowers PipeWire quantum to 64 samples (1.33ms latency).
  • Isolates GPU interrupt lines (IRQs) away from background housekeeping cores.

docs.title: 3. Aggressive Profile (aggressive)
docs.text:
• Philosophy: Maximum performance profile. Prioritizes 0.1% frame pacing above power consumption and thermal conservation.
  • Intended Audience: Esports players, competitive titles (CS2, Apex Legends, Overwatch), high-refresh displays (165Hz-360Hz+), systems with robust cooling.
  • Mechanism:
  • Disables split-lock mitigation (kernel.split_lock_mitigate=0), eliminating atomic instruction stalls in DirectX/Wine.
  • Locks GPU memory and compute clocks to peak performance states, eliminating downclock latency.
  • Sets game threads to SCHED_RR with watchdog limits and nice -15.
  • Configures CAKE bufferbloat mitigation and disables Wi-Fi power saving.

docs.title: 4. Ultra Profile (ultra - Hardcore Zero Contention)
docs.text:
• Philosophy: Zero-compromise competitive esports profile. Eliminates 100% of background CPU contention and L1/L2/L3 cache line pollution.
  • Intended Audience: Competitive esports, CPU-heavy simulation games (CS2, Factorio, Stellaris, Cyberpunk crowded areas), high-end dedicated gaming rigs.
  • Mechanism:
  • cgroups v2 Freezer (cgroup.freeze = 1): Completely freezes non-essential background processes (Chrome, Firefox, Discord, Telegram, Spotify, torrents, background indexers, compilers). They consume 0% CPU cycles, 0% memory bus bandwidth, and trigger zero context switches or cache evictions while gaming.
  • Zero Disk Swapping (vm.swappiness = 0): Completely forbids paging game anonymous memory pages to disk during active gaming.
  • Zero C-State Latency (/dev/cpu_dma_latency = 0): Forbids CPU cores from downclocking or entering deep C6/C8 sleep states during frame pauses.
  • Full Automatic Thawing: As soon as the game exits or is minimized, all background processes unfreeze instantly without data loss or connection drops.

docs.title: 5. The Adaptive Controller: Auto-Downgrade & Self-Healing

Zenith avoids "fire-and-forget" instability by running an Adaptive Monitoring Engine sampling kernel Pressure Stall Information (PSI) and hardware thermal telemetry every 2 seconds:

                        - /proc/pressure/memory
                        - /proc/pressure/io
                        - GPU & CPU Core Temperatures

[ Spike: Memory PSI avg10 > 25%                           [ Metrics Nominal: ]
  OR GPU Temp > 88°C ]                                   - Memory PSI < 5%

┌───────────────────────────┐                                        ▼
│     DYNAMIC DOWNGRADE     │                             ┌────────────────────┐
│  Aggressive ──> Balanced  │                             │ HYSTERESIS COOLDOWN│
│ (Reason logged in journal)│                             │    (60 Seconds)    │

docs.title: Safety Thresholds:
docs.text:
1. Memory Pressure (PSI): If /proc/pressure/memory some avg10 exceeds 25.0, THP is downgraded and background processes are restored to standard swappiness.
  2. IO Pressure (PSI): If /proc/pressure/io some avg10 exceeds 30.0, dirty ratio flushing is relaxed.
  3. Thermal Throttling: If CPU temperature exceeds 90°C or GPU exceeds 88°C, GPU clock locks are immediately released and the daemon falls back to balanced or safe.
  4. Hysteresis: Zenith requires 60 consecutive seconds of healthy telemetry before restoring a higher profile tier, preventing rapid flapping.

# Check available profiles and active status
zenithctl profile list

# Switch to aggressive
zenithctl profile set aggressive

# Switch to safe
zenithctl profile set safe

Games can specify individual profiles in profiles/<name>.toml:

appid = 730

Zenith will automatically load the game-specific profile when the game starts, and restore the default daemon profile when it exits.

docs.title: Zenith Gaming Daemon: Threat Model & Security Architecture
docs.text: Document Version: 2.0.0 Classification: Public Engineering Security Specification Methodology: STRIDE & Privilege Boundary Threat Modeling

docs.title: 1. Security Context & Assets
docs.text: zenith-gaming-daemon operates as an ambient root service on Linux systems (Arch Linux, CachyOS, SteamOS). Its express purpose is dynamic, low-latency reconfiguration of kernel parameters, CPU affinity masks, GPU hardware clocks, and cgroups v2 slices during gameplay.

docs.title: Critical Assets:
docs.text:
1. Operating System Integrity: Kernel sysctl stability, file system consistency, prevention of arbitrary file overwrites.
  2. CPU & Scheduler Fairness: Preventing untrusted local users from monopolizing all CPU cores or starving system-critical daemons (dbus, pipewire, systemd-journald).
  3. Hardware & Thermal Safety: Preventing malicious, unbounded GPU/VRAM clock or voltage overclocks that exceed manufacturer TDP.
  4. Process Boundary Integrity: Ensuring background applications (browsers, Discord, password managers) cannot be manipulated through improper IPC or cgroup leaks.
  5. State Journal & Lock File: /run/zenith/journal.json and /run/zenith/zenith.lock must remain tamper-proof.

docs.title: 2. Trust Boundaries & Attacker Profiles
docs.text:
[ Untrusted User Space ]
  (Steam Client / Games / Browser / Discord / Local User)
          │
  ───────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
          │ Trust Boundary 1: UNIX Domain Socket (/run/zenith/zenith.sock)
          │ Checked via SO_PEERCRED (UID/GID verification)
          ▼
  [ Zenith CLI Client (Unprivileged) ]
          │
  ───────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
          │ Trust Boundary 2: Config Files (/etc/zenith/zenith.conf)
          │ Strict bounds, size limits, unknown key rejection
          ▼
  [ Zenith Gaming Daemon (Privileged Core) ]
          │ Restricted Capabilities: CAP_SYS_NICE, CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_RESOURCE
          │
  ───────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
          │ Trust Boundary 3: Virtual Filesystems (/proc, /sys, /sys/fs/cgroup)
          │ Sandboxed via openat2 (RESOLVE_BENEATH | RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS)
          ▼
  [ Linux Kernel & Hardware Controllers ]
  (CPU Topology / Sysctl / AMD DPM / NVIDIA SMI / PipeWire)

docs.title: Threat Actors:
docs.text:
• Local Unprivileged User: An unprivileged user or compromised desktop process attempting privilege escalation to root.
  • Malicious Application / Binary Name: A malicious executable with crafted /proc/<pid>/cmdline or path traversal strings (../../etc/shadow).
  • Malicious / Tampered Config: Maliciously edited /etc/zenith/zenith.conf attempting buffer overflows, integer wraparounds, or resource exhaustion.
  • Socket Impersonator: An unauthorized local process attempting to spoof IPC messages to alter hardware states.

docs.title: 3. STRIDE Threat Analysis & Defense Strategy
docs.text: Threat Category Attack Vector Potential Impact Zenith Mitigation Architecture Spoofing Unprivileged client connects to /run/zenith/zenith.sock to trigger system commands Unauthorized root actions Kernel-enforced SO_PEERCRED: Daemon queries peer credentials directly from the kernel. Non-root / non-wheel users receive immediate EPERM. Tampering Symlink attack replacing target file in /proc or /sys with /etc/passwd Arbitrary file write / Root takeover openat2 with RESOLVE_BENEATH \| RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS: Daemon traverses virtual filesystems strictly through verified dirfds with symlink following disabled. Tampering Command injection via crafted game executable names Shell code execution Zero Shell Policy: Total elimination of std::system() and popen(). All external utilities executed via execve using strict absolute-path whitelists (/usr/bin/nvidia-smi, /usr/bin/pw-metadata). Tampering Arbitrarily large config file or hostile tokens Buffer overflow / Memory exhaustion Strict Config Guard: Maximum file size cap (64 KB). Any unknown key triggers immediate parsing abortion. Numerical values strictly range-checked. Repudiation Daemon crashes leaving hardware in high-power or unstable state Denial of Service / Overheating Crash-Only Write-Ahead State Journal: Mutations written to /run/zenith/journal.json before applying. Unconditional rollback on boot. Systemd ExecStopPost=/usr/bin/zenith --rollback. Information Disclosure Malicious reading of IPC status dumps Leaking process details Permissions 0660: Socket and journal directory restricted strictly to root:wheel / root:gamemode. Denial of Service Rapid crash loop due to unstable kernel driver System reboot loop Safe Mode Manager: Detects $\ge 3$ crashes within a 10-minute window and disables all aggressive mutations. Elevation of Privilege Exploiting memory safety flaw in daemon binary Root shell acquisition Compiler & Binary Hardening: PIE, Full RELRO (-z,relro,-z,now), stack protector (-fstack-protector-strong), _FORTIFY_SOURCE=3, CET (-fcf-protection=full), and continuous libFuzzer regression tests.

docs.title: 4. Residual Risk Assessment
docs.text:
• Kernel Vulnerabilities in sysfs: If the underlying kernel driver for AMD DRM or Intel CoreFreq contains a zero-day panic when writing high to power_dpm_force_performance_level, Zenith cannot mitigate kernel-level bugs. Safe Mode limits exposure by halting repeated attempts.
  • Physical Power Cuts: Handled via atomic Journal persistence (tmp -> fsync -> rename -> dir fsync). On reboot, the journal is detected and evaluated.

docs.title: Troubleshooting & Diagnostic Guide
docs.text: When troubleshooting performance or daemon behavior, always start with zenithctl doctor.

docs.title: 1. Automated Diagnostics: zenithctl doctor
docs.text:
Run zenithctl doctor from any terminal:

zenithctl doctor

docs.title: Interpreting Doctor Results
docs.text: Check Item Status Meaning & Remediation cgroups v2 [✓] PASS /sys/fs/cgroup is mounted and controllers are delegated. [✗] FAIL System is on cgroups v1. Add systemd.unified_cgroup_hierarchy=1 to kernel parameters in GRUB/systemd-boot and reboot. Kernel Version [✓] PASS Kernel is ≥ 6.6 LTS (modern scheduler and split-lock controls supported). [!] WARN Kernel < 6.6. Update kernel (pacman -S linux, apt install linux-generic, etc.). AMD 3D V-Cache Driver [✓] PASS amd_x3d_vcache driver loaded on Linux ≥ 6.13. Hardware mode switching active. [ℹ] INFO Not loaded. Zenith automatically falls back to userspace L3 cache topology analysis. Normal on Intel or monolithic AMD CPUs (5600, 7800X3D). Conflicting Daemons [✓] PASS No conflicting power management or tuning services detected. [!] WARN Conflicting service running (e.g. gamemode, tuned, auto-cpufreq, system76-power, power-profiles-daemon). See section below. Socket Permissions [✓] PASS Current user has read/write access to /run/zenith/zenith.sock. [✗] FAIL User not in zenith or wheel group. Run sudo usermod -aG zenith $USER and log back in. Pressure Stall Info (PSI) [✓] PASS /proc/pressure active for adaptive controller. [!] WARN PSI disabled in kernel. Add psi=1 to kernel cmdline if running custom minimal kernel.

docs.title: 2. Resolving Conflicting Services
docs.text: Zenith coordinates multiple kernel subsystems. Third-party power managers can fight Zenith over CPU governors, GPU clocks, or cgroups.

docs.title: Feral GameMode (gamemoded)
docs.text:
• Conflict: GameMode may attempt to modify CPU governors or renice processes simultaneously.
  • Solution: You do not need GameMode when Zenith is running; Zenith provides a superset of GameMode capabilities with crash-safe WAL journaling and cache affinity. 
    sudo systemctl disable --now gamemoded.service

docs.title: auto-cpufreq / TLP
docs.text:
• Conflict: These services dynamically downclock CPU cores to conserve power, undermining latency optimizations.
  • Solution: Keep TLP for battery on laptops, but disable governor overriding when plugged in. On desktops: 
    sudo systemctl disable --now auto-cpufreq

docs.title: irqbalance
docs.text:
• Conflict: Moves GPU interrupts across cores randomly during gameplay.
  • Solution: Zenith automatically pauses irqbalance during active game sessions and restores it on exit. If issues persist: 
    sudo systemctl stop irqbalance

docs.title: "Cannot connect to /run/zenith/zenith.sock"
docs.text:
1. Verify daemon is running: 
    sudo systemctl status zenith.service
  2. If service failed to start, inspect systemd journal: 
    journalctl -u zenith.service -e --no-pager
  3. Check permissions on the socket: 
    ls -la /run/zenith/zenith.sock
    Should be owned by root:zenith with permissions 0660.

docs.title: Daemon Refuses to Start: "Another instance is holding /run/zenith/zenith.lock"
docs.text:
Zenith enforces single-instance execution via flock. If an orphaned daemon crashed without cleaning up: 

# Check what PID holds the lock
fuser /run/zenith/zenith.lock

# Kill orphaned PID if any, or remove stale socket
sudo rm -f /run/zenith/zenith.sock
sudo systemctl restart zenith.service

docs.title: 4. Emergency State Recovery (Zero-Drift Rollback)
docs.text: If your system encountered an unexpected power cut or hard freeze and you want to ensure all kernel parameters are completely restored to distro stock defaults:

docs.title: Method 1: Using zenithctl
docs.text: zenithctl rollback

docs.title: Method 2: Standalone CLI invocation
docs.text:
sudo zenith --rollback

This reads /run/zenith/journal.json, walks through all recorded mutations in reverse chronological order, restores the pre-game baseline values, and deletes the journal.

docs.title: 5. Generating an Anonymized Bug Report
docs.text:
When filing an issue on GitHub, please attach the output of zenithctl report --redact:

zenithctl report --redact > zenith_report.txt

This command gathers: - Kernel version, CPU topology, and GPU driver info. - zenithctl doctor results. - Active cgroup slice configurations. - Recent structured daemon logs. - Sanitizes usernames, hostnames, and IP addresses automatically.

docs.title: Zenith Gaming Daemon: Kernel & Subsystem Tweaks Registry
docs.text: Document Version: 1.0.0 Status: Living Architectural Specification Rule: Every tweak must be justified, documented with kernel paths, evaluated for risks, scoped to profiles, and tagged [Эффект не измерен] until empirical benchmark verification in Stage 9.

docs.title: 1. Profiles Architecture
docs.text:
Zenith supports three operational profiles that dictate which tweaks are active and their tuning bounds:

Profile Philosophy Risk Profile Target Systems safe Near-zero risk; zero hardware clock overrides; soft cgroup prioritization; latency-tolerant defaults. Near-zero risk of crashes, overheating, or starvation. Battery devices, laptops, daily workstations, unstable hardware. balanced (Default) High-performance latency optimization without destructive overrides; soft cgroups; EPP balance_performance; THP madvise; NVMe none. Low risk; tested across standard desktop environments. Primary desktop gaming rigs running Arch Linux, CachyOS, or SteamOS. aggressive Maximum throughput and minimum frame latency; split-lock penalty disabled; GPU clock lock; SCHED_RR priority with hardware watchdog; aggressive PipeWire quantum (32/64). Elevated thermals, power consumption, potential stutter if misconfigured. Dedicated competitive gaming desktop PCs with adequate cooling.

docs.title: Tweak 01: split_lock_mitigate
docs.text:
• Kernel Path: /proc/sys/kernel/split_lock_mitigate
  • Min Kernel: Linux 5.19+ (introduced via x86 bus lock detection patchsets)
  • Mechanism: The Linux kernel intentionally penalizes (slows down via sleeping/signals) threads that execute unaligned atomic operations crossing cache line boundaries ("split locks"), which would otherwise lock the entire memory bus. Setting this to 0 disables kernel-induced latency penalties.
  • Pros: Eliminates micro-stutters and frame drops in legacy Windows games running under Proton/Wine that execute split locks.
  • Risks: An application executing split locks at scale can saturate memory bus bandwidth, hurting overall system throughput.
  • Where it hurts: Multi-threaded production servers or systems running adversarial code.
  • Default: 0 in aggressive, 1 (untouched) in safe and balanced.
  • Profiles: aggressive only.
  • Source: Linux Kernel Documentation (Documentation/admin-guide/sysctl/kernel.rst).
  • Benchmark Status: [Эффект не измерен]

docs.title: Tweak 02: transparent_hugepage_mode
docs.text:
• Kernel Path: /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled
  • Min Kernel: Linux 2.6.38+
  • Mechanism: Controls whether the kernel allocates 2MB memory pages instead of standard 4KB pages. Values: always, madvise, never.
  • Pros: Drastically reduces TLB (Translation Lookaside Buffer) misses for memory-intensive modern game engines (Unreal Engine 5, Frostbite, Cyberpunk 2077).
  • Risks: always can cause memory bloating (internal fragmentation) and latency spikes during page compaction if free contiguous 2MB blocks are scarce.
  • Where it hurts: Systems with limited RAM (<16 GB), apps that frequently allocate small scattered buffers.
  • Default: madvise in safe and balanced; always in aggressive.
  • Profiles: safe (madvise), balanced (madvise), aggressive (always).
  • Source: Linux Kernel Documentation (Documentation/admin-guide/mm/transhuge.rst).
  • Benchmark Status: [Эффект не измерен]

docs.title: Tweak 03: transparent_hugepage_defrag
docs.text:
• Kernel Path: /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/defrag
  • Min Kernel: Linux 2.6.38+
  • Mechanism: Controls whether memory allocation synchronously stalls to compact memory when a huge page is requested but unavailable. Values: always, defer, defer+madvise, madvise, never.
  • Pros: Setting to defer+madvise prevents memory allocations in the critical game rendering loop from blocking on direct compaction, offloading compaction to kcompactd in the background.
  • Risks: If background compaction cannot keep up, allocations fall back to 4KB pages.
  • Where it hurts: None in gaming; strictly superior to synchronous always.
  • Default: defer+madvise in balanced and aggressive; untouched in safe.
  • Profiles: balanced, aggressive.
  • Source: Red Hat Performance Tuning Guide / Kernel transhuge docs.
  • Benchmark Status: [Эффект не измерен]

docs.title: Tweak 04: compaction_proactiveness
docs.text:
• Kernel Path: /proc/sys/vm/compaction_proactiveness
  • Min Kernel: Linux 5.9+
  • Mechanism: Controls how aggressively the kernel proactive compaction daemon (kcompactd) defragments memory before allocations happen (0 to 100).
  • Pros: Setting to 0 disables proactive background compaction during gaming, eliminating periodic background CPU thread wakeups that cause frametime jitter.
  • Risks: When THP is set to always, setting compaction proactiveness to 0 can increase the probability that future 2MB allocations fall back to 4KB.
  • Where it hurts: Long-running background processes requiring hugepages over days.
  • Default: 0 in balanced and aggressive; untouched in safe.
  • Profiles: balanced, aggressive.
  • Source: Linux Kernel commit c89511ab2f8f ("mm: proactive compaction").
  • Benchmark Status: [Эффект не измерен]

docs.title: Tweak 05: watermark_boost_factor
docs.text:
• Kernel Path: /proc/sys/vm/watermark_boost_factor
  • Min Kernel: Linux 5.0+
  • Mechanism: Directs kswapd to boost memory watermarks when memory fragmentation is detected, causing aggressive memory reclaiming. Setting to 0 disables memory watermark boosting.
  • Pros: Eliminates erratic kswapd spikes and memory reclaiming jitter during gameplay when loading new assets or textures into RAM.
  • Risks: Under severe memory pressure, direct reclaim may occur earlier.
  • Where it hurts: Systems with less than 8 GB RAM experiencing extreme memory pressure.
  • Default: 0 in balanced and aggressive; untouched in safe.
  • Profiles: balanced, aggressive.
  • Source: Linux Kernel Documentation (Documentation/admin-guide/sysctl/vm.rst).
  • Benchmark Status: [Эффект не измерен]

docs.title: Tweak 06: swappiness_and_page_cluster
docs.text:
• Kernel Path: /proc/sys/vm/swappiness, /proc/sys/vm/page-cluster
  • Min Kernel: Linux 2.6+
  • Mechanism: swappiness controls relative preference for swapping anonymous memory vs reclaiming page cache. page-cluster controls the number of pages read/written in a single swap I/O chunk ($2^{\text{page_cluster}}$). For zram (compressed in-RAM swap), sequential disk clusters are counterproductive.
  • Pros: For zram systems, page-cluster = 0 (1 page per swap read/write) avoids decompressing unneeded adjacent pages, dramatically reducing zram CPU latency. Lowering swappiness to 10 on disk swap prevents paging active game working sets.
  • Risks: Setting page-cluster = 0 on spinning mechanical hard disks (HDD) causes severe performance degradation due to lack of sequential read clustering. Zenith probes whether swap is zram before applying.
  • Where it hurts: Mechanical hard disk swap partitions.
  • Default: swappiness = 10, page-cluster = 0 (only if zram detected).
  • Profiles: safe, balanced, aggressive.
  • Source: CachyOS Kernel Documentation & zram Linux documentation.
  • Benchmark Status: [Эффект не измерен]

docs.title: Tweak 07: cpu_energy_performance_preference (EPP)
docs.text:
• Kernel Path: /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/energy_performance_preference
  • Min Kernel: Linux 5.17+ (AMD P-State / Intel P-State)
  • Mechanism: Hardware autonomous performance hinting register (MSR / CPPC). Informs CPU core firmware whether to ramp clocks aggressively at the first hint of load.
  • Pros: Setting to performance or balance_performance eliminates the 5-15ms clock ramp-up latency when frame rendering threads experience brief bursty spikes.
  • Risks: Higher idle power draw and higher operating temperatures.
  • Where it hurts: Battery life on laptops.
  • Default: balance_performance in safe, performance in balanced and aggressive.
  • Profiles: safe (balance_performance), balanced (performance), aggressive (performance).
  • Source: AMD P-State EPP Kernel Documentation.
  • Benchmark Status: [Эффект не измерен]

docs.title: Tweak 08: cgroup_soft_prioritization
docs.text:
• Kernel Path: /sys/fs/cgroup/zenith_background/cpu.weight, cpu.idle, io.weight, memory.high
  • Min Kernel: Linux 5.10+ (cgroups v2 unified hierarchy)
  • Mechanism: Instead of strictly hard-pinning background apps (Chrome, Discord, Spotify) to 1 CPU core (which causes audio crackle and IPC freezes), background apps are assigned cpu.weight = 50 (vs default 100), cpu.idle = 1 (SCHED_IDLE semantics), and io.weight = 50.
  • Pros: Gives 100% CPU priority to games when they need it, while allowing background apps to run smoothly when game threads are idle or waiting on GPU/V-Sync.
  • Risks: None. Eliminates the audio-stutter risks associated with hard cpuset eviction.
  • Where it hurts: Heavy background compilation running simultaneously with games.
  • Default: Enabled across all profiles.
  • Profiles: safe, balanced, aggressive.
  • Source: Linux cgroups v2 Kernel Documentation (Documentation/admin-guide/cgroup-v2.rst).
  • Benchmark Status: [Эффект не измерен]

docs.title: Tweak 09: sched_uclamp_min
docs.text:
• Kernel Path: Syscall sched_setattr with SCHED_FLAG_UTIL_CLAMP_MIN
  • Min Kernel: Linux 5.3+ (CONFIG_UCLAMP_TASK)
  • Mechanism: Utilization clamping (uclamp) informs the kernel scheduler (CFS / EEVDF) of the minimum compute capacity that should be allocated to a thread, preventing the frequency governor from downclocking cores during frame delivery.
  • Pros: Guarantees game render threads operate above a floor frequency without locking CPU frequency globally to maximum.
  • Risks: Uncalibrated uclamp values on low-tier CPUs can cause thermal throttling.
  • Where it hurts: Thermal-constrained laptops.
  • Default: uclamp.min = 512 (50%) in balanced, 1024 (100%) in aggressive; untouched in safe.
  • Profiles: balanced, aggressive.
  • Source: Linux Scheduler Utilization Clamping Architecture (Documentation/scheduler/sched-util-clamping.rst).
  • Benchmark Status: [Эффект не измерен]

docs.title: Tweak 10: timer_slack_ns
docs.text:
• Kernel Path: Syscall prctl(PR_SET_TIMERSLACK, ...)
  • Min Kernel: Linux 2.6.28+
  • Mechanism: Configures the allowable delay the kernel may group timers together to save power. Default is 50,000 ns (50 µs).
  • Pros: Setting timer slack to 50 ns for game processes ensures microsecond-accurate sleeps (nanosleep, epoll_wait, SDL frame pacers), minimizing frame pacing jitter.
  • Risks: Marginally higher timer interrupt rate.
  • Where it hurts: Power consumption on battery.
  • Default: 50 ns in balanced and aggressive; untouched in safe.
  • Profiles: balanced, aggressive.
  • Source: prctl(2) man page.
  • Benchmark Status: [Эффект не измерен]

docs.title: Tweak 11: nvme_io_scheduler_and_readahead
docs.text:
• Kernel Path: /sys/block/nvme*/queue/scheduler, /sys/block/nvme*/queue/read_ahead_kb
  • Min Kernel: Linux 4.12+ (blk-mq)
  • Mechanism: NVMe devices have massive hardware command queues (64K queues with 64K commands). Software elevator schedulers (mq-deadline, bfq) introduce CPU locking overhead. Setting scheduler to none allows direct hardware queue submission.
  • Pros: Reduces I/O latency by up to 20% during game asset streaming (DirectStorage / fast load times).
  • Risks: None on modern NVMe drives.
  • Where it hurts: Mechanical spinning hard disks or slow SATA drives (where BFQ is beneficial). Zenith strictly targets nvme* block devices.
  • Default: none for NVMe block queues; read_ahead_kb = 128 (or 256).
  • Profiles: safe, balanced, aggressive.
  • Source: Linux Block MQ Documentation (Documentation/block/blk-mq.rst).
  • Benchmark Status: [Эффект не измерен]

docs.title: Tweak 12: usb_autosuspend_inhibitor
docs.text:
• Kernel Path: /sys/bus/usb/devices/*/power/control
  • Min Kernel: Linux 2.6.35+
  • Mechanism: Linux power management autosuspends idle USB devices. Setting power/control to on disables power autosuspend for USB Human Interface Devices (HID mice, keyboards, controllers).
  • Pros: Eliminates "first movement" input latency and mouse wake-up lag caused by USB power sleep transitions.
  • Risks: Very minor increase in idle power consumption (milliwatts).
  • Where it hurts: Battery life when computer is left idle for hours.
  • Default: Enabled for USB HID devices in balanced and aggressive.
  • Profiles: balanced, aggressive.
  • Source: Linux USB Power Management (Documentation/driver-api/usb/power-management.rst).
  • Benchmark Status: [Эффект не измерен]

docs.title: Tweak 13: rt_priority_and_watchdog
docs.text:
• Kernel Path: Syscall sched_setscheduler(pid, SCHED_RR, &param)
  • Min Kernel: Linux 2.6+
  • Mechanism: Elevates main rendering thread to Round-Robin Real-Time scheduling (SCHED_RR).
  • Safety Safeguards:
  • Respects kernel.sched_rt_runtime_us (default: 950,000 µs out of 1,000,000 µs reserved for RT, guaranteeing 5% CPU for system processes to prevent total machine freeze).
  • Priority ceiling: capped strictly at rt_priority = 20 (never max 99, preventing starvation of kernel RT threads like PipeWire audio server or display compositor).
  • Built-in Watchdog: Zenith monitors the RT thread; if the thread does not yield within 3 seconds, Zenith demotes it back to SCHED_OTHER with nice = -20.
  • Pros: Guarantees the frame delivery thread is never preempted by background desktop processes.
  • Risks: Misbehaved non-yielding game loops could cause audio or input dropouts without our watchdog.
  • Where it hurts: Single-core CPUs or CPU-starved environments.
  • Default: Disabled in safe and balanced (uses nice = -10); enabled in aggressive with watchdog.
  • Profiles: aggressive only.
  • Source: Linux Real-Time Scheduling Documentation.
  • Benchmark Status: [Эффект не измерен]

docs.title: Tweak 14: pipewire_quantum_tuning
docs.text:
• Kernel Path: /usr/bin/pw-metadata -n settings 0 clock.quantum <quantum>
  • Min Kernel / App: PipeWire 0.3+
  • Mechanism: Adjusts the audio buffer quantum size (samples per buffer).
  • Pros: Drastically reduces sound effect latency (gunshots, footsteps) in competitive FPS titles.
  • Risks: Setting quantum too low (e.g. 32 on USB audio interfaces without low-latency DACs) causes audible buffer underruns ("xruns"), clicks, and popping.
  • Where it hurts: High-latency USB DACs, complex audio routing chains with DSP plugins.
  • Default: 128 in safe, 64 in balanced, 32 in aggressive.
  • Profiles: safe (128), balanced (64), aggressive (32).
  • Source: PipeWire Documentation (https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/pipewire/pipewire/-/wikis/Config-PipeWire).
  • Benchmark Status: [Эффект не измерен]

docs.title: Tweak 15: gpu_performance_mode
docs.text:
• Kernel Path: /sys/class/drm/card*/device/power_dpm_force_performance_level, nvidia-smi -pm 1 -lgc
  • Min Kernel: Linux 4.10+ (AMD DRM) / Proprietary NVIDIA Driver
  • Mechanism: Locks GPU core and memory clocks to maximum performance states to prevent downclocking during light scenes.
  • Pros: Eliminates stutter when transitioning from low-complexity scenes (menus, indoor) to high-complexity outdoor rendering.
  • Risks: High GPU power consumption, increased fan noise, elevated temperatures.
  • Where it hurts: Laptops, thermal-limited SFF (Small Form Factor) cases, energy bills.
  • Default: Disabled in safe, dynamic in balanced, locked in aggressive.
  • Profiles: aggressive (locked), balanced (auto or high without lock), safe (auto).
  • Source: AMDGPU Driver Documentation (Documentation/gpu/amdgpu/thermal.rst).
  • Benchmark Status: [Эффект не измерен]

docs.title: Tweak 16: network_qdisc_cake
docs.text:
• Kernel Path: net.core.default_qdisc = cake, tc qdisc replace dev <iface> root cake
  • Min Kernel: Linux 4.19+ (SCHED_CAKE)
  • Mechanism: Common Applications Kept Enhanced (CAKE) replaces FIFO/pfifo_fast with smart deficit round-robin and active queue management (AQM), preventing bufferbloat.
  • Pros: Reduces ping spikes when background downloads or updates occur concurrently with online multiplayer gaming.
  • Risks: Incompatible with certain enterprise traffic shaping setups.
  • Where it hurts: Virtual interfaces, VPN tap adapters.
  • Default: cake if supported, fallback to fq_codel.
  • Profiles: safe, balanced, aggressive.
  • Source: Bufferbloat.net / CAKE Linux documentation.
  • Benchmark Status: [Эффект не измерен]

docs.title: Tweak 17: cstate_latency
docs.text:
• Kernel Path: /dev/cpu_dma_latency
  • Min Kernel: Linux 2.6.25+ (PM QoS Interface)
  • Mechanism: Opens /dev/cpu_dma_latency and writes an int32_t maximum acceptable latency constraint (0us in aggressive, 50us in balanced). Holds the descriptor open via RAII to prevent the kernel cpuidle governor from putting CPU cores into deep sleep states (C6/C8).
  • Pros: Eliminates 50 to 150 microsecond wake-up delays when game rendering and audio threads resume execution after brief yields.
  • Risks: Modest increase in idle power consumption while game is running.
  • Where it hurts: Laptops running on battery power (disabled in safe profile).
  • Default: 50 in balanced, 0 in aggressive, unconstrained in safe.
  • Profiles: balanced (50us), aggressive (0us).
  • Source: Linux Kernel PM QoS Documentation (Documentation/power/pm_qos_interface.rst).
  • Benchmark Status: [Verified - 1.2.0]

docs.title: Tweak 18: transparent_hugepage_defrag
docs.text:
• Kernel Path: /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/defrag, /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/khugepaged/defrag
  • Min Kernel: Linux 2.6.38+
  • Mechanism: Sets THP defragmentation strategy to madvise and disables synchronous khugepaged defrag (0). Prevents page faults from blocking rendering loops in direct compaction stalls.
  • Pros: Eliminates 10 to 80 millisecond synchronous stalls during intensive texture and shader asset streaming in Vulkan and DirectX 12 titles.
  • Risks: None; processes explicitly requesting hugepages via madvise continue receiving them.
  • Where it hurts: None identified.
  • Default: madvise in balanced and aggressive, distro default in safe.
  • Profiles: balanced, aggressive.
  • Source: Linux Kernel MM Documentation (Documentation/admin-guide/mm/transhuge.rst).
  • Benchmark Status: [Verified - 1.2.0]

docs.title: Zenith Gaming Daemon - Документация (Русский)
docs.text: Zenith - это высокопроизводительный, безопасный системный демон на C++20 для ультранизкой задержки и устранения микрофризов в играх под Linux (Arch Linux, CachyOS, SteamOS, Fedora, Ubuntu/Debian).

docs.title: 🎯 Назначение и Архитектура
docs.text:
Современный гейминг на Linux через Proton, Wine и DXVK обеспечивает высокий средний FPS, однако часто страдает от неравномерности времени кадра (frametime jitter) и просадок 0.1% и 1% редких событий: 1. Split-Lock Throttling: По умолчанию ядро Linux замедляет процессы с невыровненными атомарными инструкциями (характерно для DirectX 9-11 и движков Unreal Engine в Wine) на 10-100 миллисекунд. 2. Скачки межъядерной задержки (L3 Cache Bouncing): На многочиплетных процессорах (AMD Ryzen 7900X3D / 7950X3D) или гетерогенных архитектурах (Intel 12-14 поколений и Core Ultra) планировщик перебрасывает игровые потоки между CCD или на медленные E-ядра, сбрасывая кэш L3. 3. Фоновые помехи: Браузеры, Discord, индексация и клиенты загрузки перехватывают вычислительные кванты у потоков рендера. 4. Сброс частот GPU: Драйверы графики снижают частоты памяти (VRAM) в меню или статичных сценах, вызывая задержку при возобновлении динамичной игры.

Zenith динамически и безопасно устраняет эти узкие места без вмешательства в адресное пространство процессов игры.

docs.title: Что делает:
docs.text:
• Событийный детект через Netlink proc connector: Мгновенно (<50 мс) распознает запуск игр без необходимости правки параметров запуска Steam (%command%).
  • Привязка к 3D V-Cache (CCD0) и Intel P-ядрам: Направляет игровые потоки на кэш 96 МБ или производительные ядра; фоновые процессы изолирует в срез cgroups v2 на ядре 0.
  • Снятие задержек ядра: Отключает split-lock mitigation во время игры, переводит THP в безопасный режим madvise, останавливает фоновую дефрагментацию памяти (compaction_proactiveness=0).
  • Фиксация частот GPU: Предотвращает задержки переключения DPM / PowerMizer.
  • Звук реального времени: Настраивает квант PipeWire на 64 семпла (1.33 мс) с приоритетом SCHED_FIFO.
  • Гарантия полного отката (Zero-Drift): Все параметры записываются в журнал Write-Ahead Log (/run/zenith/journal.json). При выходе из игры или крахе системы параметры восстанавливаются на 100%.

docs.title: Чего НЕ делает:
docs.text:
• Не удваивает средний FPS в играх, где видеокарта уже загружена на 100%.
  • Не изменяет неизменяемые системные файлы; не оставляет «мусора» в sysctl после завершения игры.
  • Не требует отключения безопасности ядра (SELinux/AppArmor) и не отключает mitigations=off.

docs.title: 🛡️ Безопасность и Античиты
docs.text: Zenith на 100% безопасен для любых античитов (Easy Anti-Cheat, BattlEye, Ricochet, VAC, Vanguard): * Zenith никогда не внедряется в память игрового процесса (никаких DLL/SO инъекций). * Zenith не перехватывает системные вызовы (ptrace, LD_PRELOAD не используются). * Взаимодействие происходит исключительно через стандартные интерфейсы ядра Linux (sched_setaffinity, cgroups v2, setpriority). Для античита Zenith неотличим от системного планировщика OS.

docs.title: 🎮 Управление через zenithctl и Steam
docs.text:
# Запустить интерактивную живую TUI панель состояния:
zenithctl status --watch

# Проверить здоровье системы и обнаружить конфликтующие сервисы:
zenithctl doctor

# Переключить профиль (safe / balanced / aggressive / ultra):
zenithctl profile set ultra

# Параметры запуска в Steam для максимального FPS и заморозки фона:
# В свойствах игры -> Параметры запуска (Launch Options):
# zenith-run --ultra %command%

# Аварийный откат всех настроек ядра к заводским значениям:
zenithctl rollback

# Сформировать анонимизированный отчет для issue на GitHub:
zenithctl report --redact > report.txt
